A flynte stone, oute of the whiche fyre is stryken.
A people in the lasse Asia, in the countrey called Pontus, whiche people do dygge greatte plentie of yron naked. It is proprely taken for steele. And also it is the name of a fludde in Spayne.
An herbe whiche groweth in length wynding togither in dyuers partes, and hath leaues lyke to lawrel or bays, and hath a floure lyke to a vydlette, and is called of some men perwyncle.

A lyttell beaste, hauynge his skynne spotted lyke to a lybard, whych chaungeth into dyuers colours, according to the thynge that he seeth. They be ingendred in Inde, and is of the quantitie and figure of a lysard, but that his legges be lenger, and goeth vpryght, and hath a snoute lyke a swyne, a longe tayle, and small at the ende, his eyen be neuer closed, he doth neuer eate or drynke, but is nourisshed onely by ayre. Chameleon is also an herbe.
Maydens whiche were wonte to sytte at their maystresses feete.

A beaste whyche is as great as a camel, of skynne and colour lyke Panther, hauynge spottes of sondrye colours, and hath his forelegges and necke longe, and the heed lyke a camell, his fete and legges lyke an oxe.
A beaste called a camelle, communely knowen.
The countrey callyd Epirus, Chaones, men of that countrey.
A confuse matter without fourme, made fyrst of nothyng, wherof poetes supposed all other thynges to procede.
A frame, aboute the whiche vynes be wounde and tourned.
A token, a note made with a pen, a fygure, a style or fourme of speakynge.
A greatte deuowrynge byrde of the see.
The plurell numbre, is as it were a Christmas feaste, or a wake, where kynnesfolke do resorte togither, bryngyng or sendynge presentes mutually.
Charitie or loue, proprely toward men, or a mans countrey.

The graces, whiche were supposed to be the doughters of Iupiter, which were thre in noumbre, whose names were Aglaia, Thalia, Euphrosyne: And where in speakynge or writinge appered to be a meruaylous dilectation or swetenes, ir was said that therin was a grace, in latine, Charis.
A kynde of soote spyce that groweth in India.
Was named of the Paynyms, the booteman, that caried sowles ouer the three ryuers of Helle, Acheron, Stix, and Cocytus.
Paper. Also a leafe of paper, or other lyke thyng, wherin we do write. also a mayden that had neuer chylde.
A coffer, or other lyke thynge, wherin papers and rolles be kept.
The name of a man, which gaue lawes to the Atheniens.
A gulf of the see by Sicyl, wher in is daungerous saylynge, by reasone of stremes flowynge contrarye eche agaynst other, wherby shippes be therin deuourid.
A gapynge. or openyng of the firmament, or of the erthe.
The klees of a Crabbe, Crauaise, or Scorpyon.
An herbe callyd Selandine. also a westerne wynde.
A snayle. somtyme it is taken for an harpe or lute.
A maner of tombe, like to yuorie.
A parte of the foreshyp, wherby the ancre doth hange. sometyme it is taken for all the shyppe.
Is an yland, as Pompon. writeth.
A place where geese be fed.
The parte of Grece callydde nowe Morea. It is sometyme taken for the north part of the great Asia, it is also callid Chersonesus.
A serpent, whiche abydeth as well in water, as on londe.
One of the holy orders of aungelles, wherein is the science dyuine and mystycalle.
A capitayne of a thousand me.
One of the .vii. wyse men of Grece.
A gote. Also a mountayne in Lycia. Also a monster, hauynge thre heedes, one lyke a lyon, an other lyke a goote, the thyrde lyke a dragon.
A cerkle of heuen, into the whiche whan the sonne cometh, the days be at shortest.
The iuyce procedynge of meate digested, whiche by the vaynes commeth into the membres, and restoreth that whiche is consumed by heate.
An yle in the see callyd Eous, whiche was somtyme called Aeolia, where mastix growith.
He that hath suche a disease.
An obligation or lyke instrumente, wherby a man is bounden, and hath put to his hande.

The name of a man, whom poetes doo fayne to be the one halfe of a man, the other halfe lyke a hors: who fyrst dyd fynde the vertues of herbes, and taughte Aesculapius phisike, and Apollo to harpe, and Astronomy to Hercules, and was master to Achylles, and excelled all other mē of his tyme in vertue and iustyce.
Is a sore in the legges or fete, which is hote, & swelleth by the two sydes.
A facyon of gesture with the handes vsed in daunsynge, or in keruynge of meate.
A cloke, whiche proprely is worne by men of warre.
Signifieth all the greatte floodes, which be in the region of Caldee.
A certayne measure, contaynynge foure tymes the measure callyd Sextarius.
An humour callyd choler. Also a syckenes callyd the colyke.
Stuffe, proprely wherwith that place is adorned, where as shall be enterludes or disguysynges.
He that kepethe suche stuffe or apparayle.
Certayn men that lyue in woddes in Persia, whiche are soo swyfte, that they take hartes with runnynge.
The crafte to blowe trumpettes, or to playe on shawlmes, or other lyke pypes.
A fote in meetre, which hath the fyrste syllable, and the laste longe, and two in the myddell short.
A fote in meter, whiche by an other name is called trochaeus, & is but of .ii. syllables, the fyrst longe, the seconde short.
A measure to meete grounde with, or a masons rule.
The company of players or dauncers. also a quyar.
The name of a noble authour of Athenes.
A notable sentence spoken shortly, to exhorte to vertue, or disswade from vyce.
Whose colour neuer chaungeth, but is alway one.
An historie of actes done, with the tymes expressed, Cronicles.
A cytie in Phrigie, and an ylande in Indie.

r.w: Chrȳsa, Chrȳsē, An island near Crete

d: The name of a Prophete amonge the gentiles. Also of a maiden giuen by the grekes to kinge Agamēnon at the battayle of Troye.
The name of a famous and noble phylosopher.
Knyghtes that hadde shyldes of golde.
A stone with the pouder wher of paynters do make a golden colour, also goldsmythes do vse it to sowder golde.
A stone of fyrye coloure by nyghte.
Apples of the colour of gold. by an other name callid apples of Armeny.
A precious stone of the colour of golde.
The doughter of Agamemnon and Clytemnestre.
The name of a byshoppe of Constantinople, and also of an hystoryen, whiche were so called for their eloquence. for Chrysostomus is in englysshe a golden mowthe.
A certayne measure conteynynge syx tymes the measure called Sextarius.
A pot with feete, or a tryuette.
A kynd of appuls of Alexandry.
He that hath many tokens of woundes.
A token or scarre, where a wounde hadde ben.
Differeth frome Cicer oonely in coloure.
The name of the mooste noble Romayne, whyche was the father of latyne eloquence.
A fly whiche shineth by nyghte.
A lyttell leane serpent in Italy.
A byrde called a storke. also it is a certain rule or measure.
The name of him that buildid Brixis
An herbe that groweth euery where.

A venomous herbe, which groweth two cubytes in height, with a grene stalke full of knottes, bushy in the toppe, hauing leaues smaller than Coriander, and seedes greatter than anyse sede, and is horrible in sauour: Some dothe nowe vse that name for Hemlocke.
A cappe, which the kyngꝭ of Persia dydde vse, and also the byshoppes in the olde lawe.
To moue a thyng, or to cal. Bellum ciebam, They dydde sette forth to battaylle.
To moue or stirre a thyng.
Any clothe or garmente made of heare.
The ouer skynne wherwith the eye is closed.
The tēder part of the stalk of herbis.
A people called Danes. In the old tyme they inhabyted not onely Denmarke, but also all the yles frome Selande to the northe see.
People of Scythia, they that doo dwell in the countreys, where as is continuall colde and moche darkenes.
A stynkynge worme bredynge in wodde or paper.
Stones founde in a fyshes heed.
A wanton boy without shamefastnes. Also a daunser of galyardes and wanton maskes. It is also taken for a tumblar.
Heares that be trymmed. Cincinnati, men hauynge their heare trymmed.
A short cote called a ierkyn.
A shorte garment, whiche the Consulle dydde weare, whan he profered battaylle.
He that maketh hote the instrumentes, wherwith men or womenne dydde trymme their heare.
A shorte pype, hauynge a smalle sownde.
A citie of Thessaly. also the name of a Romayne, whiche exceded in crueltie.
A stone callyd a Sanguinary. it is also callyd in latyn Sanguis draconis, dragons bloudde. it is put into sondrye medycynes to staunche bloudde.
A gyrdell, whiche a bryde or newe wedded wyfe weareth, a corse.
A heare of a man or womans heed, or a medly of dyuers thinges togither.
A soote plante or herbe, whiche is good to breake and expulse the stone.
A payre of stockes. Also a lyttelle hylle, whiche menne calle a barowe. Also a tombe, a pyllar.
The name of a woman, by whome a citie in the countrey of Campania, callyd Circium, was buylded. Also a wytche, whiche tourned the companye of Vlysses into beastes.
Were certain games in Rome wherin horses ranne with chariottes.
A greate shyppe, whiche they of Asia vsed.
To compasse, to make a cerkle.

About: and it is referred somtime to tyme, as Circiter calendas Iunias, About the fyrste day of Iune. sometyme it is referred to the place. Circiter in media arce, Aboute the myddes of the castell. somtime to the thynge. Circiter duo millia hominum caesa sunt, There were nygh two thousande men slayne.
Officers in cities, whiche do go aboute to see that good rule be kepte.
A sowtherne wynd, which is wonderfulle vehement.
The serchers of watches. Also they whiche do go about the stretes to sell garmentes or lynnen clothe.
To compasse or close with a dyche, or other lyke.
By cerkles, or in the fourme of a cerkle.
He that gothe aboute to shewe hym selfe, or what he can do, or to deceyue the people.
Pertaynyng to suche auaunters or deceyuers.
She that gothe aboute to gette money with daunsynge or tumblynge.
To leade aboute, to tourne about.
To inclose, walle in, or dyche in.

To wryte, or drawe aboute with a lyne. Also to deceyue one in bargaynynge with him. Fratrē circumscripsit in diuisione haereditatis, He deceyued his brother in particion of the inheritaunce. Also to gather, comprehende, or descryue throughely. Cuius scientiae summam breuiter circumscribo, The effecte of whose lernynge I wylle comprehende or descryue shortely.
To stande about one, to defende hym.
That maye be beholden on all partes.
To inuade, or perce on al partꝭ.
To compasse a man, to deceiue hym, to close him ī, as in warres, to opp̄sse. Foenore circūuentus, Oppressed with vsury.
To dwel now here nowe there.
A place sette about with pillars.
To go aboute as a rynge dothe about a mās finger, or a diche about a close.
To cary or beare about. Also to clense. Idem ter socios pura circumtulit vnda, Vergil. 6. Also be clensed his company thre times with cleane water.
Is also to flowe or rounne aboute, as water aboute a cytie or Countreye.
That maye be, or is often caryed aboute.
Malaperte guestes and tellars of tydynges in markettes.
A Cercle. Also a rounde place walled aboute, of the whiche there were thre in Rome, where there was made certayne games.
The name of an yle in Mysia.
Heares curled, or fethers that doo growe on the toppe of abyrdes heed, as a larke or an heron.

A worme amonge corne, which I suppose to be called weuyls. Also it sygnifieth on this syde: as Cis Rhenum, on this side the Ryuer of Rhyne: Cis Alpes, on this syde the mountaynes callyd Alpes. Some tyme it sygnyfyeth lasse. Cis naturae leges, Lesse than the lawes of nature may suffre. Salust vseth it ones for beyonde. Cis Rhenū at que intra mare nostrum er oceanum, Beyonde the ryuer of Rhine, and within our see, and the occean see.
Was somtyme that countreye, whyche is frome the mountaynes callydde Alpes, vnto the Ryuer of Rubycon.
A kynge of Thrace, father of Hecuba, quene of Troy.
A cuppe or bolle made of iuy.
A precious stone lyke an yuy leafe, bright of colour.
An angle of Fraunce by Marcile, lyinge out to the see.
To cite, to sommon, or call.
A mountayne where groweth plē tie of boxe trees.
On this syde. sometȳme without. Citra adulationem, without flatterye.
A tree called a citron tree.
Quycke, hasty, swyfte. Sommetyme deuided or parted.
Is the same that ciuilis is.
A garlande of oken leaues, vsed to be gyuen to them that had saued a citesyn in battayle.
A man experte in those thinges, that appertayne to the ministration of a common weale.
A citesyn or demsen. Also Ciuis meus my countrey man.
A citie, proprely it is the multitude of cytesens gathered togyther, to lyue accordyng to lawe and ryght.
A citie in Asie the lesse.
A discomfyture in battaile, a distruction of men.
Priuilye, vnwares. Clam me profectus est, vnwaares to me, he wente his waye.
A crye, a clamour, a noyse.
The sowne of a trumpet. somtyme the crie that geese or other lyke byrdes do make.
A citie of Champayne, nere to the citie Acerras.
To appere, to be wel knowē, and to be clere.
A clerynge, a subsydie or taske graunted by a commune consent.
A riuer, whiche rounneth from the high mountaynes of Alpes, into the ryuer callyd Danubium.
An officer, which with a trūpette or tabore called people togither. sometime a man beinge in reputation.
A people or noyse of trumpettes, or belles to calle menue togither, or to goo to battaile.

A nauie of shyppes. sometyme it is taken for one shyppe. somtyme companyes or sortes of people, ordered in a citie alter the value of their substaunce. Also Classes be degrees or formes in scholes: as prima classis, the fyrste degree or fourme. &c.
To shutte a wyndowe, specially a lattyse wyndowe.
A lattyse wyndowe, or any thynge made lyke a lattyse.
An offycer appoynted to deale the emperours gyfte of money or coine amonge the souldiours.
The name of an emperor of Rome
To shytte. somtyme to compasse: also to put of: also to halte.Salustius.
A maker of kayes and lockes.
A keper of the cloyster, or of any other place, wherin any lyuyng thyng is inclosed.
A cloister, or other place, where any lyuynge thinge is inclosed.
A lyttell sentence, or a parte of a sentence.

A nayle. Also the sterne of a shippe. Also a corne on a mans toe or fingar. Moreouer, Claui be lyttell swellynges of harde fleshe in the corner of mens eien. Also puffes growing in the stemmis of great trees. Also in harneys, that whiche is callyd the ryuer. Moreouer Clauus is a garment pirled or powdred with spangles, lyke nayles heedes. wherfore the propre garmente of a Senatour was callyd Iatus clauus.
A citie of Iome, whiche Paralus buylded.
An ylande, whiche is called Marathusa.
The name of a philosopher, whiche succeded Zeno in his schole.
The name of a philosopher. there was a noble capytayne of the same name, of whom Xenophon wryteth in the expedition of Cyrus the lesse.
The name of oone of the seuen wyse men of Grece.
The name of a geometrician in the tyme of Plato.
The sonne of Pausanias, capitayne of the Lacedemons.
The name of a lady quene of Egypte.
A dyall, which dyuided the houres by the rounnynge of a certayne measure of water. It was also the name of a fountayne in Athenes.
Chosen by lotte. Also a worme, whiche distroyeth and corrupteth hony cōbes.
He that fyghtethe in iustynge harnayse.
An ouē, or the mouth of a furneis.
The nombre of clyentes or of seruantes retayned, also their offyce or dutie.
An yerely fee, for counsayle, or assystence.
Is a porcion of the worlde betwene south and north, wherin is variacyon of tyme in the lengthe of the daye, the space of halfe an houre, whiche is set oute in the tables and chartes of Cosmography
Signifyeth the degrees of mans lyfe by seuen yeres, in the whyche he is in daunger of death or mysfortune.
A ladder, and the fygure callydde gradation.
A phisition, that healeth with medicines. Also he that is so syck, that he can not aryse out of his bedde.
The name of one of the mu •• s.
A packesaddell. Also the name of a place in Rome.
Packehorses of mules, that doo serue for caryage.
A synke, whereby water passethe, or gutter.
A mayden or nymphe, whiche was maryed to Zephyrus, vnto whome was assygned for her dower, to haue reuie ouer flowers.
One of the fatall ladyes, hauynge power ouer mannes lyfe, in dyssoluynge thereof.
A cyte of Affrike, next to Cartage.
The moder of Promotheꝰ, daughter of Oceanus.
A shielde or targate of fotemen,
To ioyne togyther, or make lyke.
To gather into a kourde or creame.
To make a noyse lyke a frogge or tode.
A kynge of Sycile, to whom Dedalus fledde out of Creta, whome Minos kynge of Crete pursued.
A meate made of honye and popye sede.

o: Cocceus, a, um, et Coccineus, a, um,
n: cocceus a um et coccineus a um

d: Grayne wherwith cloth and silke is grayned.
A snayle, somtyme the shelle, somtime cokles. Also a winding staire or vyse.
A man, hauynge but one eye.
A parte of the mountayns of Alpes.
A potte to boyle in. sommetyme cocula doo sygnyfie styckes, whyche wyll soone be on fire.
A mountayne in Italy, that diuideth two sees.
Sacrifices that were doone in honour of Proserpine.
A byrde callydde a wagge tayle.
The body of a tree, or a greate boke or volume.
A dyminutife of codex, whan it is put for a boke.
An yland, that the almayns kepe.
The propre name of a kynge of Athenes, which to saue his coūtrey, willingly loste his lyfe.
He that is sycke of the colycke.
The way or crafte to ordayne a supper.
To lette a house in diuers partes to sondry persones, wherein are many parlers or drynkynge houses.
He that doth lette such houses to hyre. Vlp. de pignor. act. l. Solutum.
A parler, or other place where men do soupe.
Pertayning to suppers. Apparatus caenaucus, ordinance for supper. Sermo caenaticus, communication mete for suppers.
A lowe parler for to soupe in, a sommer parler.
To labour or endeuour my selfe to soupe.
A goer about to suppers vnbodē.
A Monasterye or other place, where men lyue in commune.
To come togither with other, to ioyne to, to drawe togyther, to gather togither, to do the acte of generation.
To restrayne, to bynde harde or straight, to compell or constrayn.
He that pleadeth an nother mannes cause, his clyent beinge present.
A surname, whiche a man hath of his auncetours.
To knowe, to consyder, to vnderstande, to lye with a woman, to iuge a matter, or here a mattier to iudge it.
To constrayne, to gather to gyther, to mylke a beaste, to make lycour thycke or harde, to presse into, to set or brynge in order.
To restrayne, to keepe of, to lette.
A company of men of warre, a courte wherin pultrie is kepte.
A thonge or lyngell, wherwith the oxe bowe & the yoke are bounden togider.
A kynde of punysshemente that is done for chastisemente.
An Ile in Asia, where Medea was borne.
A tender stalke of an herbe.
An Ilande in the occean of Inde.
A great furrowe for water to runne into, for sauynge of the corne.
He that souketh with me one norise, a foster brother.
The name of a yate in Rome
To fyght in a fielde pyghte.
Thynges writen, gathered out of many warkes.
A felowe or companyon in offyce.

To gather togyther, to take a way, to bryng togither. Seipsum colligere, Ci. Tus. 4 to brynge home agayne the partes of the mynde, that were dispersed. Also to prepare.Virgilius. Se colligit in arma, he made hym redy to fyght.
To lyne, or lay by lyne.
A hylle. also colles the backe.
An ymage as hygh and great as a towre.
To make a glade in a thycke wodde.
Whan the erthe is couered with water by greatte floodes.
To worshyp, to loue, or fauour, to haunte, to inhabyte or dwelle, to leade, Hanc uitam colo, I leade this lyfe. to tylle, or husbande grounde.
A iacket or cote without sleues.
A gutte, whiche goth from the left syde vnto the right, in the which the dunge taketh his fourme, and there is the disease called Colica, the colyke. It is also a membre or parte of a sentence.
People sent to dwell in a place, whiche is not inhabyted. Also a house of husbandrye.
A husbandemanne. also coloni be they, whiche are sent to inhabyte a countrey or towne. Also a hygh place in Athenes, where Neptune was worshypped.
The name of an yle: and also of a citie in Grece.
To make an ende, or fynishe a warke.
To gyue or make a colour.
The name of a manne that was a peynter. Quint. li. 2.
A serpent, which lyeth in the shadowe of woddes.
An ylande in the Tuskayn see.
The name of oone that wrate of husbandry moste eloquently.
The succour or staye, the wynde beame of a house.
Was in olde tyme that we calle nowe culmus.
Certayne cerkles in the celestialle Sphere.
Fygge tartes, fartes of Portyngall, or other lyke thinges.
Al the heare togyther called a bushe
To haue moche heare, or a greate busshe.
He or she that hathe a greatte bushe. By translation it is sayde of trees or herbes, that haue longe leaues or floures.
All Fraunce, a this half the mountaynes.
A boye with a fayre busshe of heare.
To burne or cōsume with fyre.
He that consumeth his own goodes ryotrously.
A companyon or felowe. Also a name of dignitie, which we cal an erle.
The daye whan people assēbled at Rome, for the election of officers.
A congregation or assemble of the people for election of officers. Also the place where the election is made.
To accompanye or goo with one, or kepe felowshyp with other.

A poynt ending a sentence, where many sentences be: as, Nihil tibi profuit nocturnum praesidium palacii, nihil urbis uigiliae, nihil timor populi, nihil concursus omnium bonorum: There is Comma foure tymes.
A saulfe conduct, or leaue to departe. sometyme vytailes for an army or multitude of menne. sommetyme for a passage of men.
That wherwith a man is remembred or recommended.
To commend or praise, sometyme to recommende.
To thynke on, to make mencyon, to dispute, to write cōmentaries, or bokes for remembrance.
A brigement or other boke, conteynynge thynges briefely writen. Also it signifieth a cōment. Also a boke of remembrance or a Register or exposition.
Fayned, or deuysed for the tyme.
A comment or exposytion, a matter fayned.
To go hither and thider, or to go to, or with an other.
An entercourse or lybertie to cary marchandyse from one place to an other. Also a commutation or forme of bieng and sellynge togither. Also a famylyarytie or custome.

To commytte. Si senserit • e timidum pater, arbitrabitur commeruisse culpam, If thy father doo perceyuethe to be aferde, he woll suppose, that thou arte gyltie,Terent. in Phor. or haste committed the offence. Also commerere, to deserue.
To goo with one to a place.
Forthewith atte hande, hande to hande.
A ioynt of any thynge that is closed and opened, as proprely of tables, whiche be ioyned.
To knocke.Terētius. Tibi uti cōmitigari uideam sandalio caput, That I may see the knocked on the heed with his slypper.

To commyt, or inioyne, to offende, to ioyne togither. Also to do and begynne.Salustius. Quibus dictis mox praeliū commisere, That spoken, they began batayle. Also to delyuer, to compare, to bring in contencion, to put togither, to confiscate or sease for a forfayture.Ci. in Ver. act. 3.
He that taketh a thynge of lone, he that boroweth.
To do for an other mannes commoditie. Also to lende.

Profite or commoditie. Also good, apte, or conueniente. sometyme it is an aduerbe, and than it sygnifieth the same tyme, in good tyme, scarsely. Commodum discesseras heri, cum Trebatius uenit, Thou were scasely departed, whanne Trebatius was come.
To be all heuy or sory.
A mayden that dothe araye or apparayle her maystresse.

To trouble, to turne or change a mans mynde. to hurt. somtyme to depart. Tu et cura, ut ualeas, et te istinc ne temerè commoueas. Farwell, and take hede that thou departe nat hense to hastily.Ci. Ty •• ,
To cōmunicate or departe some thynge with an nother, whyche I haue.
To chaunge one thynge for an other.
To chyde, or to gyue a shrewde worde for a good.
To apparayle gorgiously, to trymme, proprely it belongeth to womē.
An enterlude, wherin the common vices of men and womenne are apparantly declared in personages.
To put or ioyne togyther a thynge that is lowsed.
To compare or make equall, or more, to ordeyne, to prepare, to ioyne, to deuyse, to bye.
To compelle or constrayne, to ioyne or brynge togither.
A sauynge or sparyng, or aduauntage, a compendious or shorte fourme in wrytinge or other acte.
To deferre, or put of, or delay.
A daye ouer in matters of lawe.
To knowe of an other mā.
To fynde, or imagin in myn owne opinion.
He that hath his knees nyghe to gither, or longe fete.

To aske, or sue for an offyce, or other lyke thinge agaynst an other that dothe the semblable. Competit, It is mete or couenient. Hoc illi competit, That is mete or conueniente for hym. Also it is suffycyent.
To take by extorcyon or wronge, or as the vulgare speche is, Compilare is to polle and shaue.
To thruste. Quid faciam nunc, si tres uiri me in carcerem compegerint? Howe shall I do nowe, if the officers thruste me into prison. Sommetyme Compingere is to compact, or put togider.
Many pathes goynge into oone waye,
Feastes or drynkynges, made where as be many pathes.
To fulfylle, or fyll to the toppe, to fynyshe, or performe, to make vp. or supply that lacketh.
Imbracynge or collynge. Also agrement in wordes or sentences.
To clappe togyther the handes for ioye.
A gatter, wherin fallyth rain from many houses.
To put or ioyn togither, to make ordeine, or dispose. Also to compare, to adorne, to gather, to recreate, to appease, to conclude, to accorde or agree, to redeme, to dissemble or fayne.
He that hath his purpose or desyre. also euer content.
He that hath his own desire or appetite.
A makynge, an ornament, a composition or agrement.
To presse or thrust togither, to holde or refrayne. Also to defloure a woman.
Compellyd or hytte with any thynge.
To punche, or prycke, or stryke.
To deme, to accounte, to decerne, to impute.
A cytie of France on this syde the mountaynes, the inhabytantes wherof are called comenses.
To graunt, to permitte or suffre, to departe away, to go to a place, to consente.
A consente, many voyces in one tune, or accorde in musyke.
Any thing holowe and apte to receyue or holde, as a vessell.
A conception of a chylde within a woman. And also a conceyte or thyng conceyued in thought.

Proprely a muskle. sometyme the shell of a muskle, oyster, or cockle. Also euery vessell that is holow, and open aboue, proprely a bolle, wherin lynnen clothes be washed. somtyme a wyne vessel. Also a trū pet, as it semethe made of erthe, lyke to suche as the poore men do vse, which haue the fallyng sycknes, and do come from the place in Ducheland, called saint Corneliꝰ.
Is called a vessell of the grekes, or the holownes of the eies.
A kynde of shelle fyshe, out of the whiche a lycour is taken, wherwith sylke is dyed purple. it is sometyme taken for the purple colour.
To cutte in pieces, to die. Caesar.
To falle downe all togither. Et muri ciuitatum concidem, 〈◊〉 . And the walles of all cities shal fall all togither.
He that is redye to gyue counsayle.
A woman that endeuoureth hir to make agreemente betwene menne and their wyues.
To accorde or make frendes togither.
Counsayle, or the assemblye of counsaylours.
To make apte, or propre, or fytte.
To agre in one song, or one tune.

A pulpet or stage, wherein he standeth that exhorteth people. Also an assembly or congregation of people, callyd togyther, to here the commaundement of the kynge, or other in authorytye in the weale publyque. Also it is the oration or ꝓposition made vnto them, called a cōcion.
He that is wont to make orations or propositions to the people.
To preache or purpose a matter to the people.
He that preachethe or purposeth an oration.
To conceyue or apprehende, to delyberate, or determyne in mynde.
To swere in recyting the othe, as it is ministred.
It is at a poynte, or paste remedy.
A priuy or secrete chambre. sometyme a bankettynge chambre.
To conclude or make an ende.
A conclusyon or ende of a mattier.
To be at a cōcorde or agremēt.
To make one thynge of dyuers.
To make a greatte noyse, or to creke, as a doore dothe in the openyng.
He that medlethe with a womanne.
The fyrste slepe in the nyghte, or the depest of the nyght.

o: Concumbo, bui, concumbere, et concubo, aui, are,
n: concumbo bui concumbere et concubo aui are
d: To lye togither, to accompany togither, in the acte of generation.
A feruent desyre or appetite carnall.
To make cleanly, or honeste, to polyshe.
To appoynt, to ordeyn, to promise, to aske agayn, to denye, to assigne by mouthe, to denounce, or declare.Tit, •• . •• .
An action in the law, or appoyntment to a day certayne.
To season meate, to pouder, or otherwise order it, to preserue it from corruption.
That wherwith thynges be preserued from corruption, or elles made dilectable in tast.
That whiche is to be preserued.
Condicion, fortune, estate, election, or choyse.
He toke the bargain or promise, or he agreed.
Powderid meate, or other wise preserued.
That which may be powdered or kepte.
A Sepulchre, a place wherin ordinaunce for warre is kepte.
To laye saulfe, or hyde. sometyme to make, or buylde.
An herbe, called false dittayn, by cause it is lyke dyttayne, but it hathe lesse leaues.
To brynge with me, to hyre, to take a house or lande. also to gather, to conuert.
That whiche may be hired or taken, or is vsed to be hyred.
A swellynge in the fundement, somtyme harde, somtyme softe.
Thynges voyded or concluded by reason.
Gathered as people be gathered in a prease, thycke sette.

To put togither, to sette forthe,Plautus. to prepare, to put in. Ne posterius in me culpam conferas, Put not at the last the defaut in me. Consilia conferunt, They kepe their counsels togither. To lay to, or ioyne. Nouissima conferam primis, Terentius I wyll lay to, or ioyne the laste to the fyrste. Conferre, to profyte. Conferre in pauca, To conclude shortly.Columella Also conferre, to lay togither. Sit que utti que proximum horreum, quo conferatur rusticum instrumentū, To bothe, next there muste be a barne, wherin maye be layde vp togyther instrumentes longyng to husbandry. Also Confero, I gyue. Multa contuli in Catonem, I haue gyuen or attribute moch to Cato, I haue fauored moche Cato. Contuli me domum, I went home. Contuli me ad Catonem, I went vnto Cato.
An herbe whyche groweth in freshe waters lyke to a spunge.

To performe or finyshe,Lactātius. to perishe or be consumed, to distroy or sle, to explicate or declare. Honestatis pars cō fecta est, quā tibi cupio esse notissimam, The part of honestie is declared, which I wold shulde be vnto the perfitely knowen.Cic. offic. Also to bring to passe, Si me amas, cōfice, If thou louest me, bryng it to passe. Also to gather money. Permagnam dices ex illa re pecuniā confici posse, Thou wylt say, that a greate somme of money mought be made of that thynge. Conficere to breake.Plinius. Nucem dentibus conficere, To breake a nutte with his tethe. Also to cōsume or waste.Terentius Qui cum hic non uideant me, credant me conficere argentum suum, who bicause they se me not bere they beleue I waste their money. Also Confici, to be made. Quomodo potest ex multorum deorum aceruo unus deus confici? By what meanes maye there be of a heape of goddes one only god made?
To trust, to be sure, to dare.
He that regardeth no lawes, nor feareth any thynge. somtyme it sygnyfieth constant, assured.
Constantly, assuredly, somtime hardily, boldly, aduenturously.
A border or marche of a countrey or lande.
Places, wherinto many wyndes do blowe.
To blowe togither, to blowe lyke as one bloweth the fyre.
To stire or procure enuy, hostilitie, hate.

He is runne in dette. Also Conflare, to gather. Conflauit ex his omnibus populum, Of all those he gathered a great multitude. Also to make. Et cur uae rigidum falces conflantur in ensem, Vergilius. And the croked sithe into the harde sworde is made.
That which is apt to be wrought lyke mettall.
To be vexed or troubled, to fyghte.
To fyght as men doo in battayle.
To come or runne to gether, or flowe.
Places, in to the whiche many riuers do flowe.
Of a conformitie or lyke in facion, conueniente.
To reproue or vaynquyshe by wordes. Also to steere.
A Ryuer in Spayne, nere to a towne called Bilbilis.
To gather to gyther, or heape vppe.
An almes, or other lyberalle gyfte, giuen by the prince vnto his people, be it in money corne or vitayles.
A certayne measure, wherin Sextarius is syxe tymes, and the lycour therin conteyned wayeth tenne pounde.
To brynge or come rounde together.
To reioyce with a nother man of his good fortune.
To go with an other to fight, or dispute.
An interpretour of dremis, A Coniectour, that dothe coniecte what shall happen.
That whiche is coniectid, or gathered by coniecture.
A certayne direction of rayson vnto the trouthe.
A tree whiche beareth fruites beinge smaller at the one ende than at the other, lyke a pyne appull.
To cast into prison, or to laye a man in the stockes or gyues.
He toke hym to flight, he toke hym to his legges.
To cast dartes, or to shoote.
The chamber where the busbande and wyfe do lye.
To cōsure or conspire with other for an yll pourpose.

o: Conniueo, & Coniuo, is, iui, uel xi,
n: conniueo amp coniuo is iui uel xi
d: To winke, and is vsed to be spoken, when men wol let thynges passe, that ought to be loked on.
The female of the Cipresse tree.
The name of a kyng of Athenes.
A Canapy, proprely suche one as hangeth ouer beddes, and is wroughte lyke a net, to kepe out gnattes, whiche do stynge men in theyr beddes.
To consent, determyne, or graunt to a mattier wyllynglye.
Partie or priuy to the offence, accessarye.
They whose names be writen or registred to supply a numbre, whiche doo lacke: or suche as be newe chosen or added vnto the other.
Suche as be dedycate to one secte or opinyon.
They whiche be of one secte.
A Cōsent or accord of one mind or pourpose.
Thynges whiche do folowe or insue.
To folow immediatly, to optain, or get, to expresse. Verbis consequi non possunt, They may not be expressed in wordes.
To sowe or sette herbes togither.
Men syttynge togyther. It may be taken for a sessyons or syttynge of men, whiche be commissioners.
To sytte or abyde togyther. It may be vsed to sytte at a sessyons.
A counsayle. It may be taken for commyssioners or iudges assigned.
To stande faste or sure, to abyde boldly by a thynge.
A counsell house, specially in a princis palays.
Cousyns germains of two bretherne or two systers.
The name of an herbe, callyd Confery.
To gyue comforte, or take comforte.
To make one sowne togither. Also to accorde or agree.
A felowe or companyon, some tyme it sygnifieth lyke.
A lowpe to looke oute of a howse, or walle.

o: Conspico, spexi, ere, & Conspicor, aris, ari,
n: conspico spexi ere amp conspicor aris ari

d: Circumspect, wytty, or of a sharpe and quycke witte. Also apparant or playne to perceyue.
To conspire or consente. Also to blowe togyther.
A place where men, whanne they were bayned, layde their garmentes.
To ordeyne, to gouerne, to prouyde, to couenant, to fourme.
The complexion. Constitutio causae, whiche our lawyers do calle the matter in lawe.
To persyste or abyde in a thynge.
He is of a stedfaste mynde.
He is sure of his feete, or hoole.
It costeth, it is solde for.
To stande togyther, to be manyfeste or knowen, to agree.

To be wonte.Terentiu • somtyme to vse carnallye. Cum eius consueuit matre clanculum, He hadde company with his mother priuelye. Also to vse for a custome. sometyme to lyue.Columel • . Nec magis humo quam stagno consueuerunt, They lyue as welle on lande, as on water.
Custome or vsage. Also carnall company.
A chiefe officer among the Romaynes.
He that hadde ben consulle, or were mete to be consull.

With a datyue case, to gyue counsayle: with an accusatiue case, to aske counsaylle. Also with a datiue case, it sygnifieth to prouyde, to helpe to. Grauiter de se consulere, To doo somme hurte to hym selfe.
To gyue or aske counsayle often, to delyberate or shewe myne aduyse often.
He that gyueth counsayle, somtyme he that asketh counsayle.
The thing that is consulted. Sometyme an acte of counsaylle.
To summe vp in a recknynge, to fynishe or performe, or make vp, or make perfite.
He that dothe a thinge with consyderation.
To bourde, or to laye bourdes on a roufe or floure.

n: contagium amp contagio contagionis amp contages

d: To vyolate, or defyle, with myxtynge thynges togyther, to dishoneste.
To dispyse, or contempne, whyche is lasse than despysynge.
A beholdynge, specially in the mynde with deuocion to god.
To beholde intentifely with great affection.
They which be at one time.
He that is to be despised, or not regarded.
To contende, or resyste, or stryue, to caste or shote a darte or arow: to contynue, to make haste, to inforce.
Resystence, stryfe, or debate. Also a sharpe oration apt to confirme or repreue, a continuance, an inforcement or settynge forth with vehemence.
That whiche is contayned. also content or satisfied.
To contayn, to withhold, to lette.
To hold my peace with other. Conticesco, idem.
Bedde tyme, or the fyrst part of nyght, whan men prepare to take theyr test, and all thing is in silence.
Firme lande, that is none ile. also centynuall.
A vertue, refusing thinges that are pleasaunt. Also resistence of ylle.
To refrain, to kepe back, to contayne, to kepe togither.
Thinges wounden and twysted. Also suche matter, as oone parte can not agree with an other.
Agayn a place, a person, or a thing on the other parte.
To contrary in wordis, to saye contrary.
To goo contrarye or agaynste a thinge.
To gather togither. Contrahere aes alienum, To be indetted, to commytte, to make a contracte or bargayne, to drawe togyther. Contrahere, to shrynke. Nerui contrahuntur, the synewes be shrunken.
To lowre. Bona contracta, goodes gotten by conqueste.
Contrary, or in contrary wise. Res controuersa, mater in controuersye.
A felowe or companyon, or of one company.
Di •• bedient, or frowarde in opinyon, he that wyl not be perswaded.
Dysobedyence, a selfe wylle, or frowardenes.
A reproche, a thynge done or spoken to a mans rebuke.
He that vseth to speake rebukefully.
To breke to peces, or stryke downe.
A longe speare or morys pike. also a longe pole with yron at the ende, wherwith shypmen do gauge the water.
A valey hauynge hilles on bothe sydes.
People assembled of diuers coū treys, dwelling in one countrey or towne.
A congruence. Also a cōming togither of people.

To come togither, or to assemble in one place. Also to agree, to sewe at the lawe, or bringe in iugement. Also to determine, to speake with one, to accorde. Conuenit inter me at que hūc, it is agreed betwene him and me, De pretio conuenit, we are agreed of the price, In manū conuenit, She is my wyfe.
A congreation, most commonly for an yll purpose.
An assembly of people, warned by the chiefe officers commaundement.
May be taken for a parlyament. Minores conuentus, sessions of the peace.
The outwarde part and roūdenes of a thynge that is holowe.
A dayly companyon at table, or a dayly geste.
To feaste or bankette, or to take meales with other men.
A beden gest, he that is inuited or beden to dyner or supper.

A lyttell worme with manye feete and heary, that eateth the leaues of vynes. Also an herbe runnynge vppe by bushes, hauynge a floure lyke to a lyly, but it hath no sauoure. peraduenture that whiche is called withwynde.
Sworne bretherne, or men making one auowe or promyse.
Proprely the pyneapple tre, by trā slation it is a figure in facion lyke to a pyne appull. Also the crest of an helmet or salet.
To bushe or streke heed to heed as rammes do.

o: Coos, uel Cos, uel Co, uel Coum,
n: coos uel cos uel co uel coum
d: The name of an yle nigh to the Rhodes.
Plentie, eloquence, power, leaue, or licence, multitude.
Is rehersed, whan we wylle sygnifie to be plentie of all thinges, in that whiche we speake of.
A couplyng or ioynyng togyther, couples or fetters.
To do the office of a coke
To seethe or boyle, to make ripe, to make redy, to digest.
The herte. somtyme it is taken for the mynde.
Do not tourment thy mynde with care or heuynesse.
A cytie that Dardanus buylded, of which the inhabitantes are called Corani.
A part of the hyll Taurus.
An herbe that maketh the eies duske and weake of syght.
A parte of the hyll Taurus.
A mountayne in Asia, also a flood.
A great shippe, called a foyst.
The treasure of the temple amonge the Iewes.
Sweete harte. also wyse menne were so called amonge the Romayns.
A wytty man, and of great memorie.
It is to my mind, it cōtenteth me.
That thynge, whiche spryngeth or cometh late in the yere. Cordum foenum, latewarde haye.
The syckenesse of cattalle, whan they are clunge, that their skynnes do cleaue faste to their bodies.
Plate made of the mettal of

A citie in Achaia, which was in that parte of Greece, that is nowe callyd Morea: wherof came a prouerbe, Non est cuiuslibet Corinthum appellere, It is not in euery mans power to ariue at Corinthus, whiche doth signifie, It pertayneth not to euery man to attempt thingis dangerous, or harde to acheue. Vide originem in chiliadibus adagiorum Erasmi, uel in Aulo Gellio. Corium, the skinne of a beaste, also lether. the pane of a wall made with lyme & sande.
To make a chattryng like a choughe.
A certayne offyce in armes, concernyng capitall sentences.

o: Cornicu oculos configere, Eras. in Chilia.
n: cornicu oculos configere eras in chilia
d: To pricke out the crowes eien, is a prouerbe vsed, whan we wold signifie, that one with a newe deuise, had obscured the doctrine or estimation of them, which had ben afore him, & had made them to seeme, that they knewe or see nothing. It may be also saide, where one man wyll make all other men blynde, that haue ben before him; & reproue or dissolue that, whiche hath ben allowed by wyse men.
A garment pertainyng to souldiours. Also somtyme a towne in Italy.
Of the kynde, whyche hath hornes.
Al thing that bereth a horn.
Euery beaste that hathe horne on his feete.
A borne: by translation, the corners and wyndinges of ryuers. Also the twoo endes of a battayle be callid, Dextrum cornu, et sinistrum cornu.
Was a horne that Hercules plucked from Achelous, whiche horne the Hymphes or immortall ladyes fylled with swete flowres and fruites.
A beaste that stryketh with his hornes.
That whiche is aboue the very measure. also a lytell crowne.
A crowne, a garlande, a chaplette, a company of people standyng rounde like a cerkle. Also the cerkle aboute the mone.
A multitude of crounes, or garlandes.
A maker of crownes, or garlandes.
A towne in Greece in the partes nowe named Morea.
A cytie in the partes of Boeotia, in Greece.
The nose of a shyppe. Also an ende, the extreme parte, the toppe, the borne, or other lyke.
To crowne, or sette on a crowne or garlande.
The quātitie, state, or facyon of the body, corporature.
That which is of a bodily substance.
Corpulente or grosse in body, fleshy.
A body. sometyme it signifieth but flesshe onely. also sometyme all maner of substance.
To shaue or scrape, to take away, spoyle, sell, or alienate.
To rebuke. proprely it is to take a thinge quyckely, and with haste.
He is taken with a feuer.
Is proprely of beastes, to go togither to watrynge.
Furrowes made in hylles, to cō ney water, to washe the owre of mettall.
To corrupte, to viciate, to distroy, to suborne, to tempte, or procure by gyftes.
An Ile in the myddell see betwene Bean and the Ile of Sardinia.

A dyers fatte. Also it is the table of Apollo, from the whiche he gaue aunswere. Cato taketh it for a vessell, oute of the whiche oyle is lette runne. Also that whiche is called a corteyne of lynnen cloth or sylke. Also places deuided with cortaynes be called Cortinae.
The place where vesselles be set, wherin wyne and hony is sodden.
Or gortyna, a cite ī the ile of Cādy
The northwesterne wynde. Also a measure contaynynge .xlv. bushels.
The priestes of the Idoll Cybeles, which as madde men waggyng their heedes and daunsynge, playinge on cymbales, ranne about the stretes, prouokyng other to do the semblable.
Curious persons, crafty inuestigatours or serchers of mattiers. Also a hylle in Crete, lyenge on the see syde.
A gardeuiandes or walet, or other lyke thynge to put in vitayles.
The name of a cytie and mountayne in Sycile.
An hasyll and a hasylle nutte, or fylberde.
A bowe case, or a quyuer for arowes.
A town in Tuscan nere to Aretiū Coryza, the pose, or distillation out of the heed into the eyes and nose.
A chamberer, or woman, that apparayleth hir maistresse.
Wormes bredde in trees, which the people of Phrigia, dyd eate for a delycate meate. Also men or women that haue their bodies riueled or full of wryncles.
A tree or her be, whiche is very soote in sauour.
A touche stone, wheron they trye golde and syluer.
A hauen made with stoone. Also a towne in Byria, of the whiche a certayne kynde of smalle fygges, are called plurally, cotona, uel coctona.
A slipper, specially high corked. somtime it is taken for a hygh and arrogāt forme of speakynge or writynge.
A vessell or cuppe to drynke of, suche as Diogenes vsed, before he lerned of a chylde to drinke out of his hande.
All the holownes of a cuppe: also a measure aboute the quantytie of halfe a pynte: also the ioynte of a mans thygh. also a weight of .ix. ounces.
A place in the mountayne of Ida, out of the whiche rounneth thre great ryuers, Scamander, Granicus, & Aesopus.
Horsemen that faughte leapyng out of a chariot vnto horsebacke.
The thigh of a man. somtyme the hyppe or ioynt of the thigh.
A lyuyng togither in house, or at one table.
A great waspe, callyd a hornette.
A place of exercyse atte Corynthe.
The foremooste parte of the schulle.
An inflamation and heed ache, whiche commeth of excesse of drynkynge. It is also taken for drunkennes.
A grosse witte, which doth nothynge exactely.
To make fatte, or ful of fleshe, or thycke.
With a more playne or intelligible senes.
To deferre frome daye to daye.
Pertaynynge to to morowe, or tyme to come.
A greatte cuppe. Also a greatte hoole on the toppe of the meruaylouse hylle of Ethna in Sycyle, out of the whiche issueth flames of fyre.
The propre name of a manne, of whom Persius speaketh in his .iii. Saty.

Grates of yron or wodde. Also the name of a phylosopher, whyche to the intente he moughte the more quietely studye phylosophye, he beyng ryche, threwe all his goodes into the see, saying, Hens with a myschiefe ye vngracyous appetytes, I hadde leauer drowne you, thanne ye shoulde drowne me. Supposynge, that he moughte not haue vertue and rychesse togyther.
The name of two ryuers, the one in Grece, the other in Calaber.
A gredyron, whereon meate is broyled.
The name of a philosopher, to whom Plato wrate a boke.
To make of nothynge. Also to gette chyldren.
A creature or thinge made of nothynge.
To be wont, to be commune.
He vnto whom a man oweth any thynge.
To beleue, to truste, to cō mytte, or delyuer a thynge to be saufelye kepte, to publyshe.
Fried meate burned to the pāne.
The iuyce of barly steapyd in water, beaten and pressed,
The dentis about the leaf of an herbe or tree lyke to a sawe. Also it is the scores, whiche men vnlerned do make on styckes for their remembrance. Also Crena, is the nocke of a bowe or arowe.
The name of a king, whose daughter Iason maried, whā he had left Medea.
A shoe with lachettes, some take it for a corked shoe or slypper, bycause of the noyse, which it maketh whan a man goeth.
He that maketh showes or slyppers.
A creeke on the waters side, wheron the water beateth. Also the mouth of a well, & the extreme part of any place.
A tymbrell, or other instrument, which being touched with the hand, maketh a sownde.
To make a noyse or bounsynge.
An ornament of the beed, whiche with me • ynge of the heed yeldethe a sowne.
A bounse or great dynne or noyse.
To make a greatte noyse or sowne. Crepere, to be broken.

Tryfles or smal gyftes gyuen to lyttell chyldren, as napkyns, lyttell belles, tymbrelles, and suche lyke toyes. Also the fyrst apparayle of chyldren, as swathels, wastcotes, and such lyke. And by translation they say, A crepundijs erat uirtuti deditus. From his chyldhode he was euer giuen to vertue.
The breake or fyrste sprynge of the daye, called the twie lyght.
He is increased in his lyu • l • de, or he hath taken possession.
An Ile called nowe Candy: also a stone called Chalke.
A manne of Crete or Candye.
A buckette to drawe vp water.
A prouerbe vsed where a crafty man wyll deceyue hym that is crafty: a theefe steale from a thefe, or a lyer lye before them, whiche vse to make leasynges.
Of Crete or Candy. Also a foote in metre, whiche hath the fyrst and thyrde syllable longe.
A faulte, an offence, blame, matter layd agaynst one by action or suite. sometyme a false suspicion.
Criminalle, wherin is an offence or faulte.
To blame, to rebuke, to lay to ones charge, to accuse.
He that hath moch or long heare.
The name of a towne builded by Crisus, Phocus sonne.
He that iudgeth the actes or warkes that men do write.
The dayes wherin physytions gyue iudgement of the contynuance of the syckenesse.
Was a phisition, of whom Plinie speaketh lib .vii.
A cawle to weare on ones heed.
To make a noyse like a rauē.
A beaste in Aegypte, lyuynge somtyme in water, somtyme on lande: and is facioned in the body lyke a dragon, sauinge that he lacketh wynges.
Garmētis of the color of saffron.
A beaste in Ethiope, whiche with his tethe breaketh all thynges in pieces, & deuoureth it, be it wodde or mettall.
An instrument, whiche the Egiptians vsed in sacrifice made of .ii. plates▪ whiche beaten togither, made an harmony.
He that hath a sownynge voyce, and a shyll.
Rawe, fresh, or newe made, not type. Crudus homo, whose stomacke can not digest well.
Bloudde whiche commethe out of a wounde.
The parte of the legge, whyche is from the knee down vnto the ancle called the shanke.
The vtter parte of euery thyng that is not eaten. Also the scurfe of a scabbe or wounde, also playster of a walle.
Wheron is layde playster, or thyn shardes of stone.
A meate made of crustes of bred.
A crowst of bread, of a pasty, or of rosted, broyled, or fryed meate
Peares redde on the one syde.
A crosse, galowhowse, or other lyke.
A secrete place within the erthe.
Secrete or hydde vnder the erthe.
A place vnder grounde, with wyndowes lyke to a parler, where men do dyne in the sommer tyme for heare.
He that healeth diseasis of horses and catell.

The name of a worke man, which builded the temple of Diana, at Ephesie, a worke wonderfull, and renoumed through the worlde: the whiche was after bourned of one Herostratus, onely bycause he wold for some dede be spoken of.
A sittyng on broode, as a benne dothe.
A seruant that awayteth in the chamber: a chamberlayne, or grome of the chamber.
A bedde, sometyme it is taken for a closet.
An elbowe, sometyme a measure called a cubite, that is to say, one foote and an halfe: but a cubite in geometrie conteineth .vi. of our common cubites.
A sorsleue of a garmente, whiche keuereth the arme from the elbowe downwarde.
To lye downe, properly it is of sicke men.
Is a figure foure square on all partes like a dyce.
To make a noyse lyke an oule.
A keuerynge of the hedde, whiche men dydde vse when they walked in the nyght.
A cloke to defend rayne & winde.
A chafar, wherin water is het.
A garden where cocumbres do growe or be kepte.
A frute called a gourde. Also cucurbita, & Cucurbitula, is a cup, wherwith Surgyons do drawe out bloud with scarysying of the skynne, called cuppynge.
A place where gourdes be sowen.
To make a noyse like a cock.
To make or coyne moneye, also cudere, to breake or broyse.
A sacke, also a measure conteyning xxx. bushels.
A bolle or dyshe to drynke of.
A kechyn, sometyme the meate that is dressed.
To do the office of a cooke.
The vtter shale of a nut, whiche is grene.
An erthen cup, suche as the galye cuppes be.
The reede or strawe of corne, from the rote to the eare.
Is an offence done not weetinge, or not intendynge to do hurte.
A lyttel knife or a whittill.
Was he that kylled the beast, and diuided him in the sacrifice to Idolles. It maye nowe be taken for a slaughter man.
Apparayle, somtyme it is taken for honour done to god.

With, whan, whiles, where, albeit, for asmoche, as well. Cum mihi tum illi, Aswel to me as to him. In cum is some thing lasse vnderstande, in Tum somme thynge more. Quod cum omnibus confitendum est, tū nobis praecipue, whiche thinge oughte to be confessed of all men, and of vs moste specially. The auncient wryters, whan it sygnifyed whan, where, and forasmoche, they wrate it Quom.
Forthewith after that he hadde spoken.
He is in authoritie, or in an high offyce.
Very. Cum primis nobilis, Very noble.
A greatte vesselle, wherin corne was kepte.
An herbe and sede called cōmyn.
To make an heape, to fyll, to adde more.
In an heape, or heaped vp.
Wherin chyldren be rocked. somtyme it is taken for the age of infancy.
To tary, to prolōge tyme, to abyde, to doubte.
A tarienge, an abydyng, a prolongynge of tyme, a doutynge.

An axe to cutte woode, whiche is smalle and thyn before, and brode & thycke after, that the wodde may ryue the better. also a wedge to cleaue wodde with. By translation it is a company of fotemē in batayle, that goth in a lyke order, smal before, and brode behynde: there was a lyke forme in the Theatre or place, where men beheld playes, it is sometyme taken for a company of people.
That whiche appereth to be in the sayde fourme of Cuneus.
An herbe called sauery, wherof be dyuerse kyndes.
To dunge as a childe dothe.
An hucstar that selleth meate and drynke.
Delicate meates, or desire of deynty meates.
The sonne of Venus, god of loue. Cupido in the feminine gender, vehement desyre or appetite.
Desyrouse. sometyme it signifieth a louer.
Care, thought, study, diligence, warke or labour, also loue.

Gardeyn in socage, or he to whom the custodye of a man madde or folysshe is commytted. Also he to whom any thyng is commytted to suruey, or to prouyde thynges necessary for a weale publyke, or to order suche thinges as he hath in charge, cō cernynge as well priuate thynges as they that do belonge to a comminaltie: he maye be properly called a suruayour.
An ilande in the see Adriatike.
A littell worme in grayn called myte or wyuell. It is also the wesyll of the throte of a man, wherby he draweth wynde.
A people of the Ile of Crete or Candy.
A courte, that is to say, where the senate is, or officers exercisynge suche thinges as they haue in charge. it is sometyme taken for the persons in the courte.
They whiche be of that courte.
Also of Varro is taken for a place, where priestes consulted of thynges concernynge diuine ceremonies.

Curiouse, taken sometyme on the yll parte, where more dylygence is vsed, than is necessary or expedient: sometyme on the better parte, where we be very carefull and busy about thynges, concernynge eyther our selfes or other men.

The name of a noble Romayne, vnto whom whan the ambassadours of Samnytes hadde brought a great somme of golde for a present from theyr people, desyrynge hym to take it, and vse it at his pleasure, he answered, that Marcus Curius hadde leuer haue dominion ouer ryche men, than to be ryche him selfe, and that he, which could not be vaynquished in battayl, mought not be corrupted with money.
To care, to be doinge of a thinge. somtyme to prepare, to heale one that is sycke, to take refection or comfort.
A lyttell byrde, whiche hatchethe and bryngeth vp cuckowe byrdes.
A shorte space of tyme. Also a runnynge place.
He that hath a croked fote.
Were lyttelle carres, or drayes, hauyng in them chaires of yuorie, wherin they satte, whyche were heed officers in Rome. somtyme it is vsed of poetes for the same offycers.
Som tyme signifieth the poynte of any weapon, sometyme the stele, sometyme a speare heed.
The custody, kepynge, or warde: somtyme he that kepeth, somtyme he that is kepte, somtyme the prison.
A stone, whiche beinge broken, is lyke to a beane.
Ilandes or rather rockes vnder Thrace Bosphore.

o: Cyaneus, a, um, & Cianus, a, um,
n: cyaneus a um amp cianus a um
d: A brighte blewe colour, or blunket.
A cuppe. it is also a measure, contaynynge as moche as a reasonable manne may drynke at one draught.
Was the wyfe of Saturne, & was named of painims, the moder of the goddes, whiche hath dyuers other names, as it shall appere in their places.
A rounde place in Athenes, where thynges were sold. Also a coyne or poyse.
An auncient people, inhabitynge the yle of Sycile, which were lyke gyauntes, hauynge but oone eye in theyr foreheed.
A ryuer of Sicile, the water wherof was meruaylous colde. and as Plinie sayth, auayleable for the goute in the fete Cydon, one of the notablest townes of Candy.
An instrument, wherwith menne do beate floores, or doo ramme with. Also euery thinge that tourneth about quyckly. Also stones rounde and longe lyke beade stones, called langattes.
In the fourme of a langatte.
A hylle of Archadie, where they say Mercurius was nouryshed.
One of the names of Mercury.
A serpent that rolleth hym selfe, as he gothe.
Yonge colewortes. Also the tender parte of the stalke of euery herbe.
A pece or cup to drynke wine in.
A syckenes called the squynce, whiche is in the throte and iawes.
A sect of phylosophers, whych liued in pouerte without shame, like doggis.
A beaste hauynge the bodye lyke to an ape, and the heed lyke a dogge. Also people vnder the greate cane, hauing heedes lyke dogges.
Dogge flyes, whiche doo souke bloode from a beaste.
In latyne is canis, a dogge. Also a citie in Locris.
A thorne, the leafe wherof is lyke the steppe of a mans fote, and hathe blacke bearies like to grapes.
A figure of sterres in heuen, called Vrsa minor.
One of the names of the moone.
An herbe, hauyng leaues lyke sedges, also a rote like to ginger.
A famouse cytie in Libia. Also a citie in the yle of cypers.
The yle whiche is callid Corsica, or Corse.
A goblette to drynke wyne in.
A citie in the mountayne of Helycon.
The name of .ii. ryuers, one in Armenia, the other in Media.
The name of diuers kinges in Persi.
A kynde of yuye, that groweth alone. also the name of a ryuer.
An herbe, whiche is good to gyue to cattell agaynst the rotte.
The name of an Ile by Grece.
A countreye beyonde Hungry, on the northe parte of the ryuer of Dano, or Danubius.
A fynger, a fote in metre, hauing one longe syllable, and .ii. shorte. it is also a date.
Grapes beinge longe lyke a fynger.
The name of an excellent carpentar of Athenes, whiche fyrste founde the sawe, the twie bylle, and the awgor: and made the place in Crete callydde Laberynthus.
Whome paynyms called the god of the erthe, fyrste creatoure of the erthe.
A damned spiryte. sometyme it is taken for the sowle, beynge in the body of manne.
A spirite. sometime it is vsed for a godheed amonge the paynyms.
A countrey on the ryuer of Dano, called nowe Slauony.
One of the names of the goddesse Cybele.
To condemne, to disherite▪ to compell, to delyuer.
Harmefull, or hurtfull, or hauynge moche harme.
A philosophers name of Pythagoras secte.
A towne whiche is the boundes of Iudea, on the northe parte.
The kynge of Argyues, whiche hadde fyfty doughters, who all, sauynge one, slewe all their husbandes in one night.
A famous ryuer, now called Danowe, wherinto do flowe .lx. ryuers.
Plautus dothe vse for dant, they gyue.
A soupper, wherat be many and dyuers meates.
Delycate and precious dysshes, or bankettes.
The propre name of a lyttell maiden, and also of a wodde.
In latine is a laurell. also the sonne of Mercurie. It was also a dilectable place without the citie of Antioche, Also it was the name of a porcion of Lycia by the see syde.
One of the names of Apollo.
An herbe lyke to Laurell, now called Laureole, as I suppose.
He that bearith a dishe at a banket.
To gyue, as it were a delicate dishe.
A sacrifice, which was made in winter, and in sprynge tyme.
Forstallers of markettes, whyche do bye before hande, to selle dere afterwarde.
The name of a prince, reigning in that parte of Phrigia, where Troy stode, whiche was of him called Dardania.
The name of dyuers kynges of Persia.
The name of a kynge of Persia in the tyme of Tyberius, Caius, and Claudius themperours.
Giuen. also an officer in Rome whiche subscribed the date of letters.
One gyuyng to an other, as at the tossynge of a balle.
A parte of Italy, nowe called Appulia.

Ioyned with a verbe, or nowne, it signifieth withdrawinge or taking away, as, Decorrico, I barke or take away the rynde: Depilo, I plucke away the heare. sometyme it signifieth downeward, as Deorsum descendo, I go downewarde. Sometyme contrary, as, Dehortor, I giue contrary aduyse: Dedoceo, I teache contrary,Terentius sometyme it sygnifieth for, as, Quā tum me amas de fidicina hac? Howe well dost thou loue me for this singing wenche?
An aley to walke in, it may be somtyme vsed for a galery.
To ioynte, or to cut of by the ioyntes.
To gylte, to laye ouer all with golde.
To rage, as it were in a drunkennesse, to be wodde angrie.
To vanquyshe, or take one in battayle.
Condempned in an action of dette.
Out of the lyme kyll into the cole pitte. A prouerbe, wherby is sygnifyed frome oone myschiefe to an nother.
The boke of holy scripture, conteynynge the tenne commandementes.
A countrey in Iudea, beyonde the ryuer of slume Iordane, contaynynge tenne cyties.
To depart from a place, to mynyshe or appaire.
To goo out of the waye, or to gyue the way to an other of courteisye.
To remytte somewhat of his ryght.
The name of one of the twelue monethes.
A perche or poll ten fotelonge.
He that meateth with suche a polle.
To cutte of. also to decide or discusse a matter in variance.
Are those thinges that fall away, as leaues of trees.
Great, as Decumana porta, The great yate or entrie into a campe of an armie.
A generall receyuer or collectour of taxes or subsydies, or other lyke exactions.
To take awaye the tenthe parte from the resydue.
Was whan the tenthe persone of euery legion was put to dethe.
The tenthe, the chiefe or principalle, as, Decimum quod que ouum, Euery tenthe egge.
A grynne or trap to take byrdes.
To vnbowe, or to bringe out of compasse, or roundenesse.
The name of a noble howse of the Romaynes.
To declame, or to exercise in feyned orations.
To declare, to open a thing whiche is darke.
To eschewe, to leaue, to tourne away, to leade away, to alienate.
To stryke of a heed by the necke, also to deceyue, or disapoynte.Plautus Vna est, quae decollauit, One womanne there is, whiche hath deceyued hym.
To stayne, to spylle the coloure.
To boyle, or to sethe very moche. somtyme to chaunge, or digest perfitely. Also to consume or wast a mans substance, or to brynge detrymente or losse.
He that hath wasted all his substaunce, and is brought to extreme pouertie, speciallye by lecherye and dyse playenge.
To beautifie or make faire, or pleasaunt to the eyes or the eares, to honoure.
A semelynesse, or that which becommeth the person, hauynge respecte to his nature, degree, study, offyce, or professyon, be it in doinge or speakynge, a grace. sometyme it sygnifyeth honestie.
Decretorium sydus, wherby iudgement is giuen of the increase that shall succede of any thinge.
To lye downe, also to dye.
Tenne tymes dowbled, or tenne folde.
To double tenne tymes. If it be an aduerbe, it sygnifyeth tenne times, or tenne folde. Decúplum, like wyse.
He or she that sellethe wyne by the porte.

An offyce or dignitie, hauyng authorite orther ouer tenne men of armes, or the tenthe parte of a companye. Also it was taken for the lorde Chamberlayne to the Emperour.Suetonius in Domit. Cicero. Also they were in other cities the same that Senators were at Rome Decuria, was the order, office, or company, whiche was vnder the office of Decurio. Also the company of iuges, as we haue of the kynges Benche, Commune place, and Escheker. And Decurio, he that is chiefe of theym.
To runne downe, by translation it sygnifieth to runne from the one ende to the other.
Iustes, as at the tylte or randon.
To cutte or drawe oute in lengthe, or to cut or deuyde in ten partes.
To dedicate, or tell a message.
A renderynge vppe of a place besyeged.
Gyuen or subiecte to an other mans commandement.
To gyue vtterly, or for euer: or to become subiecte, to render vp, or yelde.
To teache a manne other wise, than he hath before lerned.
To ceasse frome sorowe, or payne.
To hewe or cutte, lyke a Carpenter.
To bryng down, or to leade, or drawe, or brynge from one place, or one thynge to an other. somtime to moue from his purpose. sometyme to bryng home honorably from any place.
To go out of the right way, or reason.
To cutte of, take away, defalcate.
To draw from the dregges, to clense or fyne.
The Eclyps of the sonne and the mone.
Sownynge or lyenge in a traunce.
To defende, to putte of, to prohybyte.
To brynge to, to disclose, to accuse, or appeale, to bestowe, to giue office or dignitie, to attribute. Deferre nomen, to complayne.
To waxe pacyente or colde, to appease hym selfe, or withdrawe his furye.
To fayle, not to suffyse, to lacke, to leaue, to disagree, to rebelle, or departe from hym, with whom he is retayned, or goeth frome one Capytayne to an nother.
Lacke, rebellion, or departing agaynste couenant or promyse.
Be that so departeth or rebelleth, or goth from one to an other.
To sette or fyxe on, or to perce or thrust through.
A definition, whyche expresseth in fewe wordes, what it is that is spoken of, as, Homo est animal, rationale, mortale, A man is a thyng lyuely, resonable, and mortalle.
He that lacketh sight in one eie.

To lack, or to be vnsufficient.Cicero. Also to forsake or fayle. Prudē tia nun quam deficit oratorem, Prudence neuer fayleth an oratoure.Caesar. Quem sanguis uires que deficiunt, whom bloode and strength faylleth. Also to forsake his capitayne, and go to his aduersary. Ab eo defecerat, He went from him to his ennemye.
To fade, or to fal away as flowres doo: or to lese beaultie. sometyme it signifieth to burgen or floure.
To flowe downeward, to fall of or away, or come to nothynge.
That whiche floweth or falleth away from any thynge.
To burye or hyde a thinge in the grounde, to dygge downe or into the erthe.
To destroye, or waste, to make in picture the fourme of a thing.
To begyle, to minisshe or take away the profyte from an other.
To rub moch, or to rub of.
To breke town, or cut down.
To consume or weare out the profite, specially of grounde, wherof shulde come corne or frute.
To vse no lenger, to leaue or resygne, to perfourme.
He that in his maners is vnlike to his auncetours, or base of lynage.
To be vnlyke to his auncetours in maners. It may be said of fruites, whiche waxe wylde.
To leade, to lyue,Plautus. to expelle, to pulle of. Degitur corium de tergo meo, The skynne is pulled of my backe.
The concubyne of Achilles, on whom he begatte Pirrhus.
To take an othe, to sweare deepely.
To throwe downe, to cast downe, to tourne away, to put out of office.
One after an other in order, from hensforth, or thensforth, afterwarde.
The name of a sonne of Priamus and Hecuba.
To vnyoke, to vnioyne, to disseuer.
To be let downe, or fal down to be consumed or wasted.
To wepe or sende out droppes lyke teares.
An accusation secretely made, or a secrete complaynt.
That whyche maye be put oute, or put awaye.
Delectation in the sēces of heryng, seinge, taste, and smellyng.
To delyte, to leade, to allure to a thynge.
Choyse or election of thinges. Also of men.
Sommetyme signifieth to take musters for the warres.
To assigne to som office message, or other necessary and great busynes, to commytte a cause or matter to be determyned, to sende in ambassade or message.
To distroy, to putte out any thynge that is writen, to remoue or putte awaye.
To be aduised, to take aduyse, to determyne, to doubte, to consult.
To taste a thynge, somtyme to vyolate, to distroy, to sacrifice, to drain water by forowes.
To pul of the barke or rind of a tree.
To be wanton, to be squaymyshe, to play the cockeney.

A wanton worde, which vneth may be expressed in englysshe, vsed betwene a man and a womā in wanton pastyme. Meum delitium, meae delitiae, my swete harte, my darlynge, my ioye, and suche other lyke, expressed best by theym that be Venus secretaries.
An offence whan a thinge is vndone, omission.
To fyle or shaue of frome any mettall.
Delectation, an allectyue, or swetenes in feelynge.
To anoynte, to rubbe pleasantly, to towche.
To drawe, as a paynter dothe, er he do lay on colours.
To omytte to do well, to offende.
Lacke. Deliquium animi, whan a man is in a swowne.
To go out of the ryght way, proprely to go out of the forow, and make a balke, as ploughmen do. Also to dote.
He that swaruethe from reason, a dotarde or dotynge foole.
A citie and people in Grece.
A greatte fysshe, called a Dolphyn.
A temple of Apollo in Grece.
A place, wherin be dyuers images of god and sayntes.
To wash cleane, or washe out.
To lay klaye on any thyng.
A place to descende into a Cellar.
To go downe, or go away.
To be madde, to make madde, to make foolyshe.
To bynde by frendship, to wynne ones fauoure, to make a frende, to deserue moche.
To meruayle moche. some tyme it signifieth to knowe not.
To send downe, to humble my selfe, to laye downe.
A fourme of a common welth,Ti. Liuius where the people haue authoritie.
He that fauoreth the cōmon welth, where the people hath auctoritie.
The name of a harper ī Homer.
To throwe downe any thing that is buylded.
That sheweth, or is shewed, or mete to be shewed.
A fourme of speakynge, wherin oratours didde either commende or dispraise any man openly.
The sonne of Theseus and Phedra kynge of Athenes.
To tary longe, to kepe back, or cause to tarye.
The name of a famous orator.
To stryke gentilly and softly with the hande, as we do to chyldren or houndes, whan we make moche of them.
At the laste. sometyme it signifieth onely, or alway.
A certayn coyne, after the diuersities of countreys, dyuers in weight. it is taken nowe for a peny.
That whiche contayneth the numbre of tenne.
To cutte or pull of the nose.
Not to gyue, or to denye to gyue.
Tenne togither. Caesar lib. 5. Vxores habent deni duodeni que inter se communes, They haue wyues tenne and twelue men togither, commune amonge them.

o: Denticulus, dentatus, ta, tum, detosus, sa, sum,
n: denticulus dentatus ta tum detosus sa sum

d: A medycyne, wherewith the tethe be rubbed, to make them white.
He that speaketh betwene the tethe, or lyspeth.
To putte forthe tethe, or breede teethe.
An instrumente, wherwith teethe be scraped.
A puttyng forth or growinge of tethe.

To shewe or tell a thinge to an other man, or denounce. Also Denunciare testimonium, to brynge wytnesse into the courte of iugement, is they doo in the Chauncerie, where wytnesses are compelled to come.
To couenant or promise or agree, or patise. Depectus, a, um, couenanted or patised. Depectus est cum hostibus, he patised with the ennemies.
To robbe a commune weale a prince, or a place halowed.
Whā monstruous or strāge thinges do happen, betokenynge some yll auēture to happen, to repele it by prayers, auowes, or other goood dedes.
To putte downe, putte away, or remoue.
To hange downe of a thing. to depende.
To be punysshed, to suffre peynes.
To perysshe, to dye, to loue inordynately.
Without hope of recouery or remedy.
To laye downe, to depriue or take away, to leaue a thynge in an other mans custody.
Layde downe, lefte in an other mans kepynge, also desperate.
To distroye or waste a countreye.
To cary or brynge awaye. to banyshe.
He that leaueth a thyng with an other man.
That whyche is lefte in an nother mannes kepynge: or that is layde to pledge.
To robbe a countrey or toune.

To beseche. Deprecari ueniā, to aske forgyuenes. Also Deprecari, to refuse, to desyre the contrary, to put awaye, or denye that whiche we wolde not haue, to haue in detestation, to resyste, to delyuer a man by prayer.
He was taken in his wordes. Deprehensus est in scelere, He was taken with the faulte. Also deprehendere to knowe, to perceyue.
To kepe down, to thrust down.
To warke a thynge with the handes, to the intent to make it soft.
A chyld or yonge beast, whiche are not come to ripe yeres.
To dishoneste or vyolate a womanne.
To clense any thing vnder fote.
To cutte of, to esteme, to iudge, to repute.
The name of a people in Asia.
A well moste colde in sommer.
To laugh, to scorn, to mock
To deriue from one to an other, to lay to one, as to lay to a mans default, or charge, to take from one, and giue to an other.
To mynysshe, to derogate, to take awaye.
A people of Grece in the costes of Thrace.
To cut or pull of that whyche is superfluous.
To be wodde angry. somtyme to ceasse to be angry.
To disagree, to leaue one and go to an other, to rebell.
To write out of a copy, to order or appoynt, to paynte or write aduysedly, to declare or describe.
To sytte styll, or contynually, to syt on a thing, to sit on a chāber stole. it is also proprely whan the erth doth gape or chinke. Terra desedit, the grounde openeth or gapeth.
Forsaken, not inhabitable, where no man dwelleth, a desert or wyldernesse.
To obey or serue humbly, somtyme to do yll seruyce.
A man ful of idelnes, slouthfull.
To assigne, to note or signinifie, to do a thinge newely.
A marshall, which setteth or appointeth euery man to his place, conuenient to his degree or office.
To do folishly, to wax folish.
That is made desolate or distroyed.
To looke or beholde downe, to despise. Despicor, caris, to dispise.
A watcheman, to se who cometh, as it is in Calyce.
To affyance or betrouth. also to promyse.
To be in desperation, or wery of lyfe, to despaire of any thynge, that a man seketh for.
To despaire, to com to great wysedom.
To skymme or claryfye any lycour.
To spet downe, or spette on a thynge.
To pourpose, to appoynte, to depute, to prepare, to chese, to tye to a thinge, to sette a pryce.

To forsake, to leaue, to depriue or take fro, to lowse, or vnbynde, to sette downe a man.Cecilius. Destituit omnes seruos ad mensam ante se, He dyd sette downe all his seruantes at the table before hym.
To distroy or throwe down that whiche is buylded.
To perce, proprely with an awle or bodkyn.
To discusse or brynge out of custome.

He that can vaunte a horse, and leape frome one horsbacke vnto an other. Also those men of warre, that in time of battaylle wolde leape downe of their horses quyckely, and fyghte on foote, and leape vppe agayne as quyckely, were Desultores.
Horses whiche serued for that purpose.
To wype of, to make cleane.
To bruse, to beate oute, as grayne is beaten oute of the eare with threshyng or treadynge.
To putte in feare, to lette by feare.
To abhore. Amonge Ciuilyons, detestari is to summon a manne with wytnesse.
Abhorryng, execration, summonyng with wytnesse, Also Apuleius takith it for geldynge.
To withholde, to restrayne from lybertie.
To bowe, to turne out of the ryght waye.
To eschue, to forbeare, to hynder by reporte or acte.
To drawe of, to report yl.
That which is cause of moche damage or hurte.
To thruste downe. somtyme to constrayne or inforce.
To put from one vessel into an other.
The name of a kynge, who in fables is sayde dydde restore mankynde distroyed with a floode.
To comme downe frome highe to lowe, from rychesse to pouertie, from prosperitie to aduersitie.
Holowe or lyke to a valaye.
To go out of the waye.
A poyse, whyche is a pounde, lackynge an ounce.
To flee or rounne frome a hygher place to a lower.
To tumble or roll downe. by translation it signifieth, it is fallē, or com from one to an other, or hapned. Deuoluta est haereditas, The īheritāce is fallē or com.
To deuoure. sommetyme to beare. Hoc taedium mihi deuorandum est, This labour I must susteyne.
A curse, a vowe to dye, or to make a man dye.
To vowe or curse, to consente to dye.
Of the right hande. somtyme it signifieth apt, conuenient, quicke and dyligent, prosperous, fauourable.
Aptnes and redynes in the thing that a man goth about.
To couple horses in a teme,
A bracelet to weare on the ryght arme. Dextrocherium the same.
Horsemenne beinge on the righte wynge in battayle.
An addicion to womens names, whan theyr folyshe louers wyl make them equall to goddesses.
The dyuelle. howe be it in greke it sygnifieth proprely a fals accuser.
A cappe, whiche an emperour or kinge weareth vnder his crowne.
A parler to suppe in. Also dyete in eatynge and drinkyng. Also a place where iugementes were gyuen.
Seruauntes that do awayte on the table. Sometyme suche as do haunt dyners & suppers, to the intent to steale somwhat.
A maner of speche, as we wolde saye diuersities in englysshe, as Northerne speche, Southerne, Kentyshe, Deuenishe, and other lyke.
Iupyter. Also it sygnifyeth of one day, as Consul Dialis, a Consul of one daye.
A lyne, whiche diuydeth any fygure into two equall partes.

The doughter of Iupyter, whyche fleinge the company of men, to the intente that she wolde not be meuyd with carnalle iustes, she contynually exercysed her selfe in huntynge wylde beastes: and for hyr chaste lyfe, she was honoured of the paynyms for a goddesse. She is also taken for the Moone.
A sprynkelynge of water, or other lyke.
A concorde in musyke of fiue tunes, and two halfe tunes.
That whiche dothe dissolue and sende forth humoures or vapours.
Is a thynne skynne or caulle in the body, whyche separateth the harte and lunges from the splene and lyuer, and is called the Myddrefe.
Prouysion for oone daye. Also a boke declarynge what is done day by day.
A distinction or poynte, whereby one worde or sentence is distincte frome an nother.
A cuppe imboced, and cunningly wrought.
Purple twyse dyed. Also a garment therof.
A cause, an accusation, a iudgemente.
A iuste Prince. Also the name of a phylosopher.
To vowe, to offre, to dedicate.
To saye, to telle, to bydde, to promyse, to affirme, to defende: as Cicero dixit causam Milonis, Cicero defended Miloes cause.
To appoynte lawes, or condycions of peace, as by the vanquysher to hym that is vanquyshed.
To sewe a man, or call him vp, (as we vse to say) by action, writte, or commandement, proprely to cause a man to be bounden to appere and make aunswere.
To make aunswere to action or playnte.
To sette or assesse a fyne or summe of money to be payde by hym, whiche hath commytted a trespace.
To gyue commandement or sentence on a peyne. Sometyme it sygnifyeth to gouerne by lawes a towne or countrey.
To take an oth. proprely as they do, whiche be retayned in warres.

The hyghest offyce in the publyke weale of the Romaynes, whiche was also called Magister populi, the mayster of the people: whiche for the space of syxe monethes, hadde the authoritie of a kynge. And therfore that dignitie was neuer giuē but onely whan the state of the citie was in any ieoperdie.
The office or dignitie of dictator.
A citie in the yle of Crete or Candy.
Tauntes, or quippies, or short and sharpe reasons.
A worde, a forme of speaking.
To speake ofte or in dyuers places.
To speake or declare that an other writeth, or beareth in remembrance. Also to inuestigate or expounde the sence of any authour. Also to brynge to remembraunce.
Interpretations, exposytions, or declarations, made by maysters vnto their scholers.
To goo aboute, or prepare to speake.
One of the names of Diana.
A hylle, wherein the temple of Diana was sytuate.
One of the Centaures, and an hystographier of Candy.
The name of a lady that buylded Carthage.
To brynge into sondry partes, or to diuide or pulle aparte.
Ylandes of Aphrike, that bound • on Aegypte.
The name of a man, and in latine it signifieth Geminus, in englyshe, a twinne or double.
A daye. Sometyme it sygnyfyeth tyme or season.
The dayes in whyche phisitions do gyue a certayne iugement in syckenes.
It is daye, it waxeth daye.
Amonge lawyers be callyd ordinary dayes, or dayes in courte.
One of the names of Iupiter.

To spare or deferre. sometyme to brynge frome one place to an nother. somtime to report abrode, somtyme to deuide or cut asonder, somtyme to set in order. sometyme differ or be in difference. Cic. At uide quid differat inter meam opinionem & tuam, But se nowe what difference is betwene thyne opinion and myne.
To vnbuckle, to open, to vngird.
To diffine or declare in few wordes playnely, the sygnyfycation of a thynge.
A diffinition, or declaration of the nature qualitie or propre sygnification of a thynge by generaltie, specialtie, and difference.
To flye asonder, or on dyuers partes.
Amonge lawyers, to contynue the matter vntyll an other daye.
Amonge latynes is the letter F.
