A iustyce of gayle delyuery, or any Iustyce, whyche dothe gyue sentence on theues.
A senatours robe or garment. it is put somtyme for the dignitie of a Senatour. semblably Laticlauium.
A synke, wherinto fowle water is caste or swepte, wherby pauementes are made cleane.
An yle in the see called Pontus.
To prayse. Laudo testem, I take to wytnesse.
A goddesse, vnder whose protection theues were in Rome.
A citie in Italye, called also Lautentum.

o: Lauo, uaui, are, & lauo, ui, ere,
n: lauo uaui are amp lauo ui ere

d: A leafe of a laurell or bay tree, sometyme a garlande made of Laurell.
A manne of the towne callyd Laurentum.
A citie in Italy callid also Lauiniū.
To put on a garlande of laurell.
A crowne or garlande that vyctours ware in theyr triumphe.
A place, wherin doo growe laurelles or baye trees.
He that wearethe a garlande of laurell.
A place in Attica, where syluer was dygged.
Were presentes, which the Romās did send to ambassadors of other realmes.
Magnifycence and netenesse in dyners and bankettes.
Washed. also nete or cleane, or elegant, ryche.
To lowse or sette at lybertie, to release.
Was in batayle, whan the sondry bendes or companyes of fote men were set in a ray, one man a cōuenient distance from an nother, that they mought fyght the more at their lybertie.
An Ilande by Cyrenaica, a regyon of Affrike.
A thynge lyke to bed, wherin riche men, and noble men were borne by six seruantes. It may be taken for a lyghter.
A diuination or prophecy by the noyse of basons.
A chaumberlayne, or he that maketh the beddes.

A solemnitie among the paynims whan in the honour of their goddis Iupiter, Iuno, and Minerua, beddes were spradde in the temples, in the which fyrst the idolles were layde, in the resydue as many as mought lye and eate.
A part of Asia, lyenge into the see.
A bedde. Lectulus, a lyttell bedde.
A potte of erthe, whiche serued onely for oyle.
To whome any thynge is bequethed.
He that bequetheth any thing, the testatour.
An ambassadour, that hathe commissyon to treate of matriers. He that is sente oonely to salute or congratulate, is callyd Orator.
A company of men of warre, cō taynyng cōmonly, syxe thousand fote mē, seuen hundred thyrty and two horsemen.
A maker or gyuer of lawes.
Dayes in banke, whanne the partie shulde appere or pleade.
Iugementes confirmed by lawes written, or auncient custome.
To sende as an ambassadour, or as a legate, or deputie, to commytte, or appoynte, to bequeathe.
To gather, to rede, to passe by to stryke.
All maner of pulse, as beanes, peason, vetches, tares. &c.
People, whiche were alway wandrynge, and dwelled sommetyme in Thessalia.
A ryuer whiche runneth into the ryuer of Rone.
A swyfte lyttelle shyppe, whyche may be callyd a barke.
An yle in the see called Aegeum.
That whyche is nowe callyd Terra sigillata.
Spyrites, whyche doo walke by nyght with horrible fygures.
One of the names of Bacchus.
To pacifie, to appease, to treate gentilly, to make plain, or smoth, to cōforte.
That whiche hath no roughnes, meke, tractable, softe of condicions.
Mekenesse, gentilnesse, easynesse to please, softenes, smothenes.
A baude, a marchant of hoores.
The practyse of bawdry. sometyme immoderate and exquisyte clenlynes or elegancye, to styrre a manne to vyce.
To practise baudrye. Also to speake fayre, or allure oone with wordes, and other pleasaunt thynges.
A kynde of poulse called fatches.
A maner of vessel, out of the whiche kynges and princes were annoynted, a Chrismatorie.
A thynge lyke a lyttell warte in the face redde or blacke.
A lyttell tree, out of the whyche cometh Mastix, a swete gumme.
To doo a thynge softely or easyly, slowely.
Softe, gentylle, easye, slowe, remysse, ydell, cleauynge, or clammy.
Idem. Also a lytel fishers bote.
A prouerbe touching thē, which be sowre of countenance, fierce, & vncurteyse.
Spoken where one attēpteth a thynge dangerous, and almost impossible.
The name of an excellent grauer.
The ꝓpre name of a philosopher.

Was kynge of the Lacedemonians, whiche dyd feates of warre agaynste Xerxes kynge of Persia incredible, and finally was slayne in defendyng Grece, with foure thousande and eight hundrid grekes onely, against .xvii. hundred thousande of the hooste of Xerxes. There was also an other Leonides, which was tutour to king Alexander, whan he was a chylde.
An herbe, whiche groweth on hilles, whose floures are like to a lions mouth whan he gapeth.

An herbe, hauynge leaues lyke to colewortes, the stalke halfe a foote high, the sede in huskes as great as smalle peason, the rote lyke a rape rote, great and blacke, whiche helpeth ageynste the styngyng and bytynge of all maner of serpētis.
A lyttell worme, whiche if the lyon do byte, he dyeth incontinent.
A lyttell beaste, whose heed is tourned into asshes, wherwith men doo myxte fleshe, and cast it in the ways, wherby lyons do passe, wherof if they doo eate, they dye incontinent.
An herbe callid Pee de lyon whiche hath floures lyke roses vnspradde.
An herbe lyke to a wyld parsnippe.
Nete, polyte, and pleasaunte, as well in speeche, as in gesture.
Purenesse or netenesse in speeche. Also the good grace and dilectablenesse in speche and gesture.
An inclosure,Varro .3. de re rust. or place inclosed, wherin are kepte any beastes for pleasure or huntynge.
A l • uret or yonge hare.
A place, wherein the citie of Argon layde all their ordure and fylthe.
Of Lerna. Lerna malorum. the dunge heape of mischiefes.
An Ilande in the see Icarie.
An ile in the see called Agaeum.
A lamentable voyce, vsed in the burieng of men, us we do saye, Alas.
A people in the extreme parte of Italye, whiche dyd eate the companyons of Vlysses, rostynge them on broches.
A syckenes, whiche causeth one to slepe continually, and to forget al thing.
He that hath the slepynge or forgettynge syckenesse.
A ryuer of hel, the water wherof as soone as it is drunke, causeth a man to forgette all thynge that is passed.
A promontorie or elbowe of lande, nygh to Corinthus.
An herbe, which phisytions of late dayes calle Camomylle.
A mountaine in Epiro. also an yle.
A littell towne not far from Smirna.
A browne or a russette coloure.
He that dothe weare a russet garment.
A countrey, whiche is now called Cappadocia.
An yle agaynste Pestanum, in the the see Thyrrhenum.
The goddesse, whiche was called Matuta, & Aurora.
One of the sonnes of Iacob, the patriarch.
A dragon of the see: it is taken in holy scripture for the dyuell.
Thynne wrought, and of small substance.
To lyfte vp. somtime to take away, to abate.

Lyght. Also whan it is spoken of worldly thynges, it sygnifieth lefte, vnhappy, contrary: whan it is referred to celestiall thynges, it betokeneth ryghte, fortunate, prosperous. For that whiche to vs is the lefte hande, to them, whiche are aboue vs, and do looke towarde vs, is the ryghte hande.
The peculyar lawe, whyche euery citie hath.
A lawe, whyche assigned howe many persones shulde be boden to souper, and that men shulde soupe at their doores, to the intent that it moughte appere, howe the lawe was obeyed.
Medycines, whyche doo heale menne of feuers.
People in hyghe Fraunce aboute Burbon.
Be holes in the toppe of a maste, whiche doo receyue the cabulles, or roopes.
An yle in the Indian see.
A taste or say taken, proprely in sacrifice.
The name of a great Rhetorician.
A wynde, whyche dothe blowe out of the northweste.
A mountayne betwene Araby and Phenicia. It is also a tree, whyche bryngeth forthe incense.
Maysters of the requestes, whiche do receyue billes of supplication, being put in, to the kyng or prince.Hieron.
A lyttell boke: also sometyme an epistell, a supplication, a lybell or declaration in the lawe, of dette, trespasse, couenant, and other lyke.
One of the names of Venus.
The fynder of wyne, called also Bacchus & Dionysius.
Free, at lybertie, not bounden, large, or greatte.
A boke or warke writen, the inner rynde of a tree.
Lyberall. Liberales artes, the lyberall sciences, or sciences belongynge to a free manne.
Where a man contendeth for his lybertie.
Chyldren, as well women as men.
To delyuer, to sette at lybertie.
To content, or satisfie hym, of whom money is borowed.
Lybertie taken alwaye in the good parte.
He that of a bondeman is manumised or infranchised.
A caue, wherin was a well, callyd
Where the Muses beinge conuersant, were therfore called Libethrides.
The Muses, or ladies of sciēces.
A moūtain in Macedonia, where the Muses dyd dwelle.
Sensualitie, vnlefull appetite or luste. Sometyme it sygnifieth onely appetite or wylle.
A goddesse, in whose temple were solde all thynges pertaynyng to sepulture or funeralles. sometyme for burienge. Also for dethe, or the beere, wheron deade bodyes are caryed.
He that hath the suruayeng and charge aboute burienges.
To tast any thing: somtime to touche, somtyme to sacrifice, somtyme to take.
A pound weight: somtyme a payre of balaunces. it is also one of the .xii. sygnes.
Conteined a hūdred dragmas, and was called Mna, or Mina.
Contayned .xii. ounces, that is to say foure score & syxtene dragmas,
Pertaynynge to bokes, or of a pounde weyght.
The hanging equally of the balance.
A cogell or stone, to throwe at one.

A weyer. It was also amonge the Romaynes he, whiche bought a bondman or slaue, takynge a pounde weighte of brasse in his hande, and sayeng: This man, whiche with this money and brason pound is boughte to my vse, by the lawes of the Romayns. I say, is myn owne.
To way, to poyse, to make weightye, to houer.
A wynde, the whiche bloweth out of the southe.
People of the countrey called Liburnia, also commune messangers.
A part of Galmatia, or Slauony.
A lyght shyppe, as a barke or galias.
A citie in Iudea, on the easte parte of the ryuer of Iordane.
Stones, which ar not very clere,
It is lefull. sommetyme it is vsed for maye. Mihi licet, I maye. Tibi licet, thou mayste. sometyme be it so, admytte it.
A measure, whiche excedethe not foure fyngers.
A foule breakyng out, whyche begynneth aboute the chynne. Some do take it for the frenche pockes.
Be thredes, whiche sylke women do weaue in lyncelles or stooles.
A weauers shyttel, or a sylke womans tauell, wheron sylke or threde beinge wounden, is shot through the web or lome.
A chepener, a chapman, sometyme it signifieth a broker.
To bye and selle for gaynes, or to bargayn by exchaunge or cheuisance, to fyght, to deceyue a manne by a craftye bargayne.

A sergeant, or other lyke minister to execute corporall punyshement. A Consul of Rome had .xii. other heed officers: syx which bare euery one in their handis, roddes and axes bounden togither, to do with them execution, as they were cōmaunded.
Pertaynyng to sergeantes and other lyke officers.
A tyle in lengthe one foote and an halfe, in bredth one foote.
A ryuer in France called Loire.
The countrey in Italye, where the citie of Geane is sette.
To eate lycorousely, or to deuoure sweete or dayntye meates. Also to eate daintily or curiousely.
A daintie feder, an eater of delicate meates.
Of the countrey of Liguria, a Ianuens of Ianeway.
The see that is by Ieane.

A tree, which dothe beare white floures, and soote: wherof is made an oyle called oleum cyprinum: and this tree doth growe in watrye places, as wyllowes and salowes do. It is also an herbe, which some men do cal Maior, and groweth by hedges.
Are people of Asye, whyche with Xerxes warred agaynste the Grekes.
An hyll in Sicile on the see banke. Also a towne.
A place where do grow many lilyes.
A snayle. Also a man, which prieth or seketh for some thynge to consume.
A maker of gardes or purfils.
A purfyll of a womans garment, or a garde of a mans garment.
Signifyeth not only the thrassholde of a doore, but also the haunse, somtyme it signifieth the entre of the dore. somtyme frendeshyppe, after the expolytion of Seruius.
Sygnifieth a bounde or butting in fieldes.
Feldes lyeng in the extreme marches of a countrey.
Souldiours appoynted to kepe the borders of a countrey.
To bounde or lymitte how ferre a thynge doethe extende.
A vesture from the bely downward. Also mudde or slime, which is in the water.
To looke wantonly on the one syde, to caste a wanton eie, to loke a skewe.
A carpenters lyne or corde. it sygnifieth also euery line generally, either made or ymagined to be.
To lycke with the tunge. also to sucke downe by lyttell and lyttell.
A tongue. also a language. Also an instrument, wherwith men do take medycines or salues out of a boxe.
A lyttell tunge. Also a lachet or lingell. Also Lingua & lingula, do sommetyme signifie a spoone.
A great speker, ful of wordes.
A woman full of wordes. Also a fyshe called a soole.
To annoynte or laye on somme thynge, that is thycke. also to lyne.
An herbe, whyche is also callyd Marubium.
A ryuer and towne in Campania.
A shete. It is taken for all lynnen clothes. sometyme for sayles.
Lytell botes made of holowe trees.
He that brought fyrst letters out of Phenicia into Grece, and was mayster to Hercules.
A beaste, whiche hathe the face of a lyon, the body spotted lyke a panther, and is of the greatnesse of a doo, whose vryne is sodaynly tourned into a precyous stone.
An yle by Greece. It is also a softe playster.
A soundyng, where one semeth to be deade.
To be porreblynde, or sande blynde, or dymme of syght.
Scrappes, or leauynges of vitayle, or other thynges.
To be liquide or soft, as oyle.
To discouer, or make to appere.
Lyquide runnynge & softe. sometyme pure, also prosperous.
To runne out, as lycour dothe.
A rydge of lande, whiche is ouer the surrowe. sometyme it sygnifyeth an harpe.
To assesse damages and costes for the playntyfe in an action.
Where oae medleth in an other mans matter, as it were his owne.
A letter. Literae, a letter or letters that be sent. sometyme it signifieth sciences.
Was in the olde tyme, A, as betokenynge absoluynge, Litera tristis, B, as sygnifyenge condemnynge.
Blynde letters, whyche eyther in defaulte of the ynke, or of the parchemente, or for auncientie, maye not be radde.
A grammarian, or a mayster of grammer.
A blower of a smalle trumpette.
A cement, wherwith stones are ioyned togyther.
An herbe, which hath sedes lyke stoones, and groweth amonge corne: whyche herbe curethe the stoone of the bladder.
A place paued with square stoones.
To varie, to stryue, to sewe one an nother.
To please god with sacrifyce, and to optayne my desyre.
The bankes, as well of the see, as of a great ryuer. somtyme lande butting on the see callyd the see syde.

n: littoreus rea um amp littoralis littorale

d: A blottynge or stryke through that, whiche is writen, cancellynge.
To blotte or stryke throughe, or cancelle.
A croked staffe, which the diuinours called Augures, helde in their handes, whā they appoynted places in their diuination. Also a scepter, and a trumpette.
He that hath his skyn blacke with beatynge, also enuious.

The coloure, whiche is lefte on the skynne, after beatynge or whippynge.Lucanus. somtyme it is taken for enuye. Liuor edax tibi cuncta negat, The gnawyng enuie denayeth the all thynges.Claudius lib. 3. Rabiem liuoris acerbi Nulla potest placare quies, No quiete canne content the ragynge of bytter enuy.
A skullyon, whiche carieth wodde or water in an hoste, or to the kychen.
He that for a smalle rewarde dothe moste vyle seruyce.
Lye made of ashes to wasshe clothes cleane.
A braunche of the grayn callyd Millium.
The hyre of a house or lodgyng.
He that letteth house or lande, a lessour.

To set or lay, as a howse is set in a place, a foundation is layde. Also to laye vp, as a thing is to be kepte. Sometyme to gyue in mariage. Also to lette a thynge to hyretor to rent, to make a lease.
A citie in the vttermoste parte of Italy, whiche was named Magna graecia.
People of Locrus. there were also people so named in Grece.
Places made with bourdes, wherin tame culuers, and other byrdes or conyes are kepte to brede.
A lyttell place. Also a purse, an almorie, a lyttell coffer, a biere, wheron deed bodies are borne to be buried.
To make ryche of yerelye reuenewes.
A place. somtime a family or kinred. also slede, as Loco patris te habeo, I take the in stede of my father.
The secrete partes of a womanne.

A flye with longe hynder legges, whiche bourneth corne with touchynge of it, and deuoureth the resydue. In India be of them thre foote in lengthe, whiche the people of that countrey do eate. It is also a see fishe, like to a creuys, called a lopster.
A taunt or reproche in scoffyng.
A blaste of wynde tourned frome the erthe vpwarde.
Logike, one of the lyberal sciences, the c • a • t • of reasonyng or arguinge.
A place where iuges gyue sentēce: also a gathering of rent, or other reuenues
He that speaketh craftily to deceiue: or in eloquente wordes induceth sentences vayne, or of lyttell purpose.
A contencion with wordes, or an vnd •• rete altercation.
Vsed for a latyn worde, is taken for triflynge wordes, or vayne language.
A fyshe, which hath his heed betwene his fete and his bealy: and hathe also two bones, one lyke a knyfe, the other lyke a penne.
A wiede growynge in corne, callyd Cockyll.
A regyon of Italye, callyd Lumbardye.
A gutte, out of the whyche ordure issueth.
An aduerbe, signifieth longe, farre, excedynge.
A drynke made of grapes, after that they be pressed, callyd Seconde.
Seruantes whiche serued to bynde men, or to beate them, whan they were by their maisters commaunded.
An haberion, a place made vppon walles lyke an open galery, with grates of tymber or hurdels, to kepe men frome fallyng. It is also the walle plate, before that morter is layde on it.
In warfare is a munymēt or fortification, that the besigers of cites do make.
Whose fete ar, as if they were bounden or gyrte.
A thonge of lether, or a colar, or other lyke thynge, wherewith beastes are bounden or tyed. sometyme a whip, wherwith a man or beaste is whypped.
A countrey betwene Pycardye and Normandy.
People in Affrike, whyche doo lyue by eating only of a frute, callid Lotos.
Is a notable tree in Affrike, or herbe, of whose fruite if a stranger do eate, he dothe incontinently forget his owne countrey.
One of the names of Apollo.
Myrthe, pleasantnes, moste proprely in wordes.
Slypper, waueryng. sometyme redy to slyppe or slyde.
A citie in Italye, of whiche the inhabytantes are called Lucenses.
Were taken of the olde latines for Elephantes.
A countray belongyng to the royalme of Naples.
People of the countrey of Lucania.
A pouddynge made of porke, • sawsage.
A famous poete, which wrate the battayle betwene Cesar and Pompeye.
Money bestowid in woddes, dedicat • to goddis, called Luci.
Feastes, whiche the Romains made in holy woddes.
A lyttell gayne, a small markette.
That whiche hath his lyghte of an nother thynge.
The thirde parte of the people of Rome, distributed by Catius & Romulus.
A kynge of Ardea, whiche holpe Romulus agaynst Tatius.
To be bryght or clere, as day.
One of the names of Iuno.
That whiche is light of it selfe.
To make clere, or to gyue lyght.
Whyche fleeth frome lyghte, and delyteth in darkenesse.
The name of an olde poete.
One of the names of the mone, called also the goddesse of byrthe.
They whiche haue lyttell eyen, and smalle syghte.
An hylle in the countreye of the Sabynes.
He that fleeth frō lucre or gaines
A mere or great water in Cāpania.
A couetous manne, an inordynate gayner.

n: luctor aris ari amp lucto are

d: Weepynge and waylynge, the habyte of mournynge,
To make any thynge by candelle lyghte.
The name of a noble Romayne.
A hygh and thycke wodde, somtime it signifieth lyght, whan it is of the fourth declination. It is also a citie in Spayne by Compostella, which is now called Lucensis.
A mocke, or any thynge that is mocked.
Any play or pastime, or an enterlude
Players in enterludes or stage playes.
To playe, to mocke or deceiue in game. Opera luditur, The warke or labour is loste.
Play in actes, myrth in wordes: also a schoole or place of exercyse.
Pestilence in men, murrayn in beastis.
A citie in Fraunce, callid Lions.
Pertaynynge to mournynge. Vestis lugubris, a mournynge garment.
He that is madde or sycke at a certayne tyme of the moone.
To haue the heed stryken of.
A female wolfe. also an harlotte.
A place dedicate to Pan, the god of shepeherdes.
A wolfe. Also a bytte for a hors. also a hoke to drawe vp thinges our of a pyt. Also a kynde of spyders.
A prouerbe, whan he cometh, whiche is spoken of.
A prouerbe in thynges that be daungerous, eyther to retaine, or to lette goo.
A deuourer of his own substāce
He that seeth playnely by nyghte.
Porblynde. sommetyme a man hauynge but one eye.
Pertayning to riot and lechery. sometyme a thynge done euery fyfte yere.
The day whan a chylde is fyrst named, whiche in men chylderne was the nynth day, in womenne childern it was the viii. day. It may nowe be vsed for the daye of christenynge of chylderne.
To go aboute in circute, to make satisfaction by sacrifice, to consyder in the mynde, to shadowe, to beholde aboute.

A denne or caue of wylde beastes in woddes, an hidde place and vyle, a hous where gluttonye and lecherie is haunted, also the hauntynge of the same vices: sometyme it sygnifyeth the space of fiue yeres. Also the generall purgation of the citie by sacrifice euery fyfte yere.
A cuppe, wherin wine is delayde with water
The colour of yelowe, approchinge towarde redde, of the colour of the yolke of an egge, or of waxe newe made.
A lytell floure of the colour of yelowe, in greatnes and sauour, not moch vnlyke a vyolette.
A beuar, or a beast moche lyke to it, whiche gnaweth trees asonder. and dothe haunte greatte waters, and lyueth lyke an Ottar.
Whose bones are out of ioynte.
To excede, to abunde more than is necessarie in the body or personage.
To abounde excessiuely in thynges concernynge the mynde or goodes: Also to be wanton with to moch welth or prosperitie.
To prosperouse, or lyuynge in to moche pleasure.
All superfluitie or excesse, as well in carnalle pleasure, as in sumptuous fare, apparayle, or buyldyng.
One of the names of Bacchus, called god of wynes.
Was the schole of Aristotell in Athenes.
A mountayne in the countreye of Archadia.
The kyng of Archadia, whom Iupiter tourned into a wolfe.
A countrey in Asia: after somme writers, it is a parte of Archadia.
People in Asia the lesse,Ptho. li. 3. nere to Lycia, as writeth Ptolome.
An herbe whose floure shyneth by nyght, and fyrste springeth, and longest dureth: whiche in drynke helpeth them that are stongen with the Scorpion.
They whiche do tourne the daye into nyght, and the nyght into daye.
A matche of a candelle, sometyme the selfe candell.
A countrey in the lasse Asia.
The name of a Centaure, and of a shepeherde in Vergile.
A thyng made with the iuyce of an herbe, wherwith soore eis be cured.
A dogge commen of a wolfe and a dogge.
One of the names of Apollo.
A kynge of the Lacedemoniens, whiche gaue to them their fyrste lawes.
A ryuer in the countreye of Caesaria.
A royalme in Asia the more.
The flyxe or continuall lowsenes of the bealye.
A madde man, which lyke to a wodde dogge, runneth hither and thither.

Was a manne, who (as Varro writeth) coulde see shyppes on the see .Cxxx. myles from hym, & dyd nombre them. And some wrate, that he coulde see throughe a walle. And therfore they, whiche haue very sharpe syghtes, be sayde to haue
A citie atte the Rodes, where they dyd sacrifice to Hercules with reproches and curses.
A beaste lyke to a wolfe, hauynge many spottes, whose syght dothe perce all thynges. It is also a byrde, whyche hath a tongue lyke a serpente.
A Capitayne of the Lacedemonyans, a man contentious, whiche dydde sette all Grece in the Lacedemonians top, and was slayne of the Thebans.
An oratour moste pleasant, of whom Quint. speaketh.
A noble man of Macedony, the scholar of Callisthenes.
A worme in a dogges tongue.
The name of a manne. In latyn it sygnifieth blessed.
The name of certayne noble menne, whiche were capitains of the Iewes.
A realme ioinyng to Grece, whereof the great Alexander was kynge.
A man or womā of Macedony.
A vittayllour or seller of all maner of vittayle.
A place where all maner of vytayle is solde. Macellus is somtyme taken for a leane man.
To make softe with lyeng longe in lycour.
A wall of stone without morter, made in the stede of an hedge. also leannesse.
Spoken of the body, signifieth to make leane, or thynne, or softe by steapynge in lycour: referred to the mynde, it sygnifieth to vexe or inquiete.
The sonne of Aesculapius, an excellent surgeon.
A thynge craftilye inuented, or a crafty inuention, an engyne.
To inuent craftily, to deuyse, to ymagine.
A ryuer, whiche rounneth betwene the mountaynes of Liguria.
People of Aethiopia, whiche do lyue very longe.
The name of a great lerned mā.
He, whiche hath greatte chekes, and a gapynge mouth.
To slee or kylle: also to beate, sometyme to honour.
An hutche, wherin breade is putte: some doo calle it a brake, wherwith dowe is wroughte.
A spotte, a blemyshe: Also infamye or reproche. Sometyme the masshe of a nette or hole betwene the thredes: also a nette, images wrought in marble.Varro.
A citie set in the boundes of Getulia and Numidia.
To weate, to washe, to bain.
To sweat, or be through wet.
A citie beyond Arabia on the south part in the desert of the Sarasyns, ageinst the caste parte of the redde see.
A certayne kynde of white vynes.

A ryuer of the countray of Phrigia, whiche hathe many tournynges and wyndynges: and of that all crooked and subtyll tournynge wayes, meanes, and deuyses, be called Meandri. There is also of that name a mountayne in India.
A citie in the realme of Thracia.
A kynde of great crabbes of the see.
A fyshe, whiche I suppose we do calle a Menowe.
Women, whiche dyd alwaye folowe Bacchus, with their heare scatterid like mad women, running hither & thither.
One of the names of Bacchus.
Is a countrey in Asia the lasse, callyd also Lidia.
Of Maeonia. Homere the excellent poete was named Maeonius, eyther bicause that he was borne in that coūtrey, or els that his fathers name was Maeon.
A greatte mere in the countrey of Scithia, whiche is alway frosen.
Loke after in Maereo et Mereor.

Magike, whiche is in two sortes, one is the secrete knowlege of the naturall qualyties and hydde operations and causes of thynges, and that is called Magia naturalis, naturall magike: A nother is superstionie & deuillishe, called witche crafte, sorcery, or other lyke detestable names, whiche is vnlefull by the lawes of god and man.
Kychen bourdes, or instrumentes perteynynge to the kechyn.
The dignite or office of a master.
A great offycer, a man hauynge autoritie in gouernance of people. all be it that some haue more authoritie by the lawes, and some haue lesse.
The chefe ruler of the people, by the whiche name the Dictatour amonge the Romaynes was called.
A master or teacher of sciēces.
An offycer lyke to the mayster of the rolls.
Confections made of dyuerse sweete spices in paste only for the sauour, as pomaundres and washing balles. somtyme it is taken for the dreggis of sweete oyles.
That parte of Italy from Larentum to Cumas.
Gret thinges to be wondered at.
Valiantnesse of courage or harte, magnanimity.
A noble man, a mā of great estimation.
A disposition and administration in doinge or makynge of great thynges and sumptuous.
A kynde of Caules called also Laserpitium.
Signifieth in the Persiane tongue a wyse man, expert also in the misteries of theyr ceremonyes, sometyme it signifieth a witche.
To confirme the astate of princes dignitie.
To lese the preeminence of princes dignitie.
Calme of the See, also the griefe of the stomacke not susteynyng meate, abhorrynge all thinges, as a womanne with chylde, some do cal it the abhomination of the stomake.
A stone of a dark grene colour.
A kynde of malowes.Plaut. i • Epi.
A mollifienge playster, wherby hard impostumes be made soft or ripe.
To make softe or rype. Also to exercyse.
A promontorie or hylle lienge into the see by Laconia, which is daungerous for shyppes to passe by.
To be yll reported of, to haue an yll name.
To haue yll opynion of one.
Yll handled, yll intreated.Ci. in Ver. Brutus i • Cice.
A wytche, whiche with sorcerye dothe hurte to her neyghbours.
Damage, wrong displeasure, hurt, a myscheuous dede.
To gyue ylle language to one.
Yll intreated, yll handelyd, shrewdely welcome.
Coste lost, he on whome a man hath lost al that he hath bestowid. Fugitiue prodi, male conciliare, Come forthe mycher, on whome I haue loste all that thou costest me.
I am yll or soore aferde.
I am sorie or yll apayde for that mattier: or that mattier greueth me soore.
I am yl vexed, I am il at ese.
God sende hym yuell lucke therof, yll maye he brooke it.
The rynde of a pome granade.
To beare malyce, to be hatefulle.
Wycked, cruell, enuyous, & couetous, maligna uia, an yll way.
Grounde that is ylle to be broughte to tylthe.
Wickednes, malignitie, enuye, malyce, vnprofytablenesse, the vyce contrarye to lyberalitie.
Contrary to vertue & goodnes. somtyme it signifieth subtiltie with deceyte.
A lyttelle hammer. It is also a smalle boughe or twygge of a vyne. Also Malleoli be sommetyme taken generallye for smalle stickes.
A basyn, wher in menne do washe their handes.
A swete oyntment, wherwith men were wont to washe their heare.
I had leauer, or rather: mauis, mauul.
Whiche in latyn is callyd foliū, is a swete herbe growing in India, vpon waters without any roote.
A clay, whyche touchynge anye other mattier or substaunce, settethe it on fyre.
An appull tree of the femynyne gender.
In the masculyne gender, a maste of a shyppe.

Beinge an aduerbe,Terent. in Phor • . sygnifieth with a myschiefe, or like thyng. Quid uo • malum ergo me sic ludificamini? Than wherfore with a myschiefe do you thus mocke me. Quid tua (malum) id referi? what with a myschiefe reckest thou therfore, or hast thou therwith to do?
Yll, contrary to good: somtime labour, vexation, sycknesse, grefe, malice.
To gyue the dugge or breste to a chylde.
A womanne with greatte dugges or breastes.
A kerchefe, wherwith women do couer theyr pappes.
In the language of Syria, worldly substaunce, rychesse.

n: mammosus sa amp mammeatus ta tum

d: A certayne bread vsed in Syria, whiche ere it be throughe baken, fallyth into coles.
To droppe or stylle out, or runne out softly. also to descende, to procede.
In the olde tyme, was taken for Bona, good.
An Ilande in the northe parte of Britannia.
He that byeth or hyreth any thynge of the people.
That which is solēnely bought before wytnesses. Also a mannes propre goodes or catell. sometyme a bondeman.
The solempne fourme or maner of byenge any thynge before wytnes, by lyuerye and seyson, or possessyon takynge, with other thynges executed, requysyte for the assuraunce of any bargayne & sale.
The assuraunce by lyuerye and possessyon.
The principall takers of lande, or other thynge, wherof groweth yerely reuenues. Also they, whiche doo take on them to perfourme any worke in greatte.
To gyue or selle a thynge with warrantie.
To take a thynge with warantie of hym, the whyche gyueth or selleth it.
The interest or right of a thinge.
To delyuer in bondage, to delyuer possession, to make lyuery & sayson.
To be his owne manne, and none other mans subiect or seruant.
To delyuer possession, reseruynge a rente.
To take possession or lyuerye and saison.
Lackynge one hand. also generally that, whiche lacketh any thyng necessary.
He to whome commaundemente is gyuen.
A commyssion. Also a commandement, a charge.
A • awebone, wherin the teethe be sette.
To cōmitte, memoriae mandare, to remembre, to put in remembraunce, to leaue in memorie, or for a memoriall.
To wryte a thing, to the ••• ent to be in perpetuall remembraunce.
To put a man in truste with a thynge. Mandare teriae semina, to putte sede into the grounde.
To chewe meate, or grynde it with the tethe.
A great eater, or he that is alway eatynge.
A cabin, a shepehouse, or oxehous.
An herbe callyd Mandrag, whiche beareth a lyttell apple: the iuyce whereof dronken or smellyd to, causeth a manne to slepe.
Imagis caried about in pageātis with great chekes and wide mouthes.
To abyde, to tary, to persiste, to happen hereafter.
A place to abide in, also a poste place, for conuayinge of letters or other thynges spedyly.
The good and badde aungell. Some tyme they be taken for deuylles, somtyme for spyrytes or sowles, not pourged of synne, sommetyme for the peynes, whiche soules do suffre.
Was taken for a seller of childerne to abhominable vses. It is also taken for suche one as polyssheth or paynteth a thynge with a fals colour, to selle it the deerer.
The crafte to make thynges saleable:
To polysshe, paynte, or trymme a thynge, to make it more vendible, or to be better solde.

Is where in a parlyament, greatte counsayle, or other great assembly, to haue the consente of many men, the greatter parte consentyng to one mannes opinyon or sentence, to goo towarde hym, holdynge vp theyr handes, in token that they be therevnto agreed.
Sleues of a garmente. Also manacles to tie the hādes togither. Also gantlettes and splyntes, and myttaynes, or longe gloues.
A secte of heritikes, so callyd of an Archeherytyque called Manychen.
Thynges, whiche doo abyde in remembraunce.
Iles agaynst India, beyonde the ryuer of Ganges, where as be rockes of Adamant stones, which do drawe to them shyppes that haue yron nayles.
An handefull, a grype, a bende of men, proprely of tenne souldiours.
A standerd bearer, or baner bearer.
Cruelle gouernaunce or rule, without any mercy.

A delycate meate, whiche god sent to the Iewes beinge in the deserte. also a sweete dewe, whyche falleth in the mornynges, and lyethe on leaues congelyd lyke whyte hony, whyche phisicions do vse for a medycine to purge coler easily.
The pouder or duste that cometh of frankincense.
A balle of leade to throw. also the caster therof.
To runne oute, as lycour dothe: also to droppe out, to appere out, as sweat out of the poores.
Mekenes, gentylnesse, a moderate temperance betwixte pride and symplicitie.
Meate, whiche the nourices doo chewe, and after giue it to the chyld, puttynge it into his mouthe.
A great eater: also ripe and apt to be eaten.
A towel wherwith menne do wype their handes, whan they haue washed. Also a cloke.
A place where dyuels in ydolles gaue aunsweres.

A beast which is in India, in body like to a lion, but more rough, hauynge a face like to a mā, & in his mouth .ii. rewes or set of teeth, the raile of a scorpiō, & the voyce of a smalle trumpette: and is of colour redde, and wyll neuer be made tame.
A stealer of napry, also a pike pours, or cutte pourse.
Towels or other lyke thyngis wherwith men do wype their handes.
To do a thynge slyly, as to pike a purse.
Amōg the old writers to abide.
A noble citie in Italy, where Vergile the excellent poore was borne.
The pray taken of ennemies: also money, for the whiche the pray was solde.
The hylte or handle of a weapon or instrument.
A prouerbe, sygnifienge, Leaue whiles it is wel.
To ioyne in battayle, to ioyne in issue, whan one sueth a nother.
To lerne as scholers do in the scholes.
To manumyse or infraunchise a bonde man.
To chalenge right or propretie in a thynge, it maye be taken for derayning of battayle in a wryte of ryght, after the lawes of Englande.
A hande, a grapul to fasten shippes togither, somtime it signifieth a multitude of men in the ayde of one, sometyme power, sometyme writynge, also the nose or snoute of an olyphant.
Attachement, also saisen or saisure of a thing, wherunto we make title.
A felde in the countrey of Athenes, and also a towne there.
An herbe, whiche is called fenell or fenkill.
An yle wherin is abundaunce of fenell, and it is also called Clazomenia.
People in Germany, whiche are nowe supposed to be either of Boeme or of Morauia.
A Ryuer in Egipte, also a parte of Libia, a parte of Epirus.
A perle, a Margarite: sometime generally all preciouse stones are called Margaritae. Plinius.
The brymme or edge of euery thynge, the margent.
Vnsauery fygges, wylde fygges, fygges which do open, that the sedes do appere, also great piles in the fundement.
Of the see syde, or of the see.
A propre name of a man.
An hyll in the yle callyd Parus.
Shyps or barges vsed in Media.
Callyd god of battayle. some tyme it is taken for battayle.
Of his owne propre wytte, with out any counsayle.
Borne vnder the planet of Mars.
A fyelde at Rome, dedycate to Mars.
To be manly, great, or wyse, to be come of the male kynde.
A mountayne, whiche diuydeth Parthia from Aria.

A people in Asia, whiche rounnynge on horsebacke throughe desertes, doo drynke their horses bloudde myxte with mylke, they also doo eate theyr parentes, if they die for age: but if they be sycke, they caste theym to wylde beastes to be deuoured.
Kynge of Numidia, and greate frende to the Romaynes.
A countrey in the southe parte of Spayne.
A cite in hygh France, callid Marsiles.
A countreye in Affrike, amonge the westerne Moores.
A knaue worthye to be beaten.Plautus 〈◊〉 trucule • Plaut.
A felow worthy to be whipped. Also certayne ministers, which with whyppes remoued the people, where there was moche prease.
A teate. also a cesterne, whereinto water doth runne, and eftesones runneth out by a cocke or spoute.
A garment, whiche men of Sardinia vsed to weare.
To touche dishonestly the priuy membres of a man.
The name of a famous lawyer, whiche wrate on the lawes ciuyle.
An vrinall, or other vessell, seruyng to that pourpose.
The vanitie, whiche is in a science or crafte.
An houswife, goodwyfe of the house, she that hath gouernaunce of other women, be she maried or vnmaried.
She that is a mother, & hath mother lyuynge.
Matter, wheerof any thyng is made, be it mettal, wodde, stone, erthe, or any thynge elles.
That which is of som matter.
A frenche speare, or a iauelyn.
He that is cunnynge in aulgryme, musyke, geometry, and astronomy.
The solemne feastes of Matuta, called the mother of goddes.

The mother or matrice in a woman, in the whyche the chylde is conceiued. also matrix is any female kynde that concenieth and beareth. Also the citie in a countrey, where as is the archbishops see is callyd matrix vrbs, whiche in greke is callid Metropolis.
A wyfe. also the name of a ryuer in Burbon.
The sonne or doughter of my mothers syster.
Quickely. Iube marurate illam exire huc, Byd her come for the quickely.
Tymely, nor to soone, nor to late.
Rypenes in all thynge, and as it were perfection.
To make rype or perfyte, to do a thynge perfectly in due tyme & measure: sometyme to do a thyng spedily or quickly.
Rype, perfite, somtime it signifieth aged. Maturus homo, an aged man.
Moriske, or the countreye of Moores.
The king of a realme callid Caria

A sepulchre or tombe, whiche Arthemisia made for her husbād Mausolꝰ, which for the excellent warkmanship was accoūtid to be one of the meruailes of the worlde, & for the famousnes therof, euery gret & notable sepulchre is callid Mausoleū
A cake made of floure and mylke.
A cytie in Cappadocia vnder the hyll callid Argeus, nowe called Cesaria.
A ryuer in the mouthe of the see, called mare Hircanum.
A platter wherin meat is caried
A fourme of swearynge, as who sayth, so Castor helpe me.
Minion to Augustus the emperour, and bicause he was the supporter of great lerned men, all fauourers and succourers of lerned men be so called.
A kynde of letuse, which causeth a man to slepe.
In greke, is popye in englyshe.
With me. Mecū facit, it maketh for my purpose. Mecū sentit, he is of min opinion.
Wyfe vnto Iason, a witche and cruelle womanne.
Wordes whiche maye be taken in a good or ylle parte, as tempestas whiche signifieth tempest and tyme, facinus, a notable dede good or ylle, ualitudo, helth, or syckenes, and other lyke.
That which is in the midle.
A drudge or lubber, which doth in the howse all maner of vyle seruice, as swepe or clense the house, carie wodde to the kytchen, and other like drudgery.Budeus.
The seruant, whiche hath the rule of the hous vnder his maister.
An herbe, whiche specially nourysheth horses, and ones beinge sowen, eftesones springeth ten yeres continually, and commonly it is called Sylla.
In state to be healed, curable.
A medicine. sometyme it sygnifieth poyson.
A certayn measure of corne, cō taynynge syxe tymes the measure callyd modius. Vide modium.
The chiefe citie of Lombardy, callyd Myllayne.
An instrumente, wherwith ropes are made.
Studiousely,Plautus in • tich. in Bacch, perfectelye on the fyngers endes.
A thynkynge or dyuysynge in thought. also an exercise, aswell of minde, as of bodye.
In the myddel of the lande, and furthest from the see.
To thynke deepely, and in thynkynge to fynde out, to purpose, to lay snares, to synge or playe swetely.
Ceremonyes vsed by theym, whyche dranke muste or newe wyne.
The myddes equally distant from the extremytes. sometyme meane.
A meane or mediatour betwene .ii. menne.

An othe, whiche althoughe somtyme it had a nother signification, yet may it nowe in a commune fourme of spekynge be vsed in this wise, by the faythe of my body: sens Dius for Iupiter, and fidius for filius, be nowe out of vse.
A Ryuer aboute Venyce, called nowe Brent.
To take out marowe, somtime to expresse vtterly. Narraiam rem nobis omnem, ati que emedulla, Tell and expresse vtterly to vs all the hole matter.

A lady, of whom fables do report, that her heares by Minerua were tourned in to adders, and they which behelde her were tourned into stones: whom Perseus afterward slewe. she is somtyme taken for one of the furtes of hell.
Priestes of Diana, whiche alway were gelded.
A furie or turmentour of hel, whiche Paynyms supposed dyd prouoke and •• ere men to woodnes.
The festiual day, dedicate to Cybele, called the mother of goddes among Paynyms.
Playes to the honour of Cybele.
An honourable facyon in gyuynge or imployeng of great thynges, whych besemeth a man of great courage.
He that doth great thinges accordynge to his dignitie.
A Cytie belongynge to Athenes. It was also the name of oone of Hercules wyues.
Whome we doo calle nobles or pieres of the realme.
A fyshe hauynge a blacke taile.
The leane partes of the fishe called Tunny.
A wanton worde spoken by louers vnto their paramours, my litel hony.
Byrdes, whiche we doo calle hennes of Genny.
An yle in the Venecian see.
A kynde of faukons very lytell of body, black and puissant, which haunteth mountaynes, and feedeth her byrdes alone, a merlyon as I suppose.
A soore or skalle in the heed lyke a hony combe, out of the whiche cometh an humour lyke hony.
Whome the gentyls dyd honour for one of the goddes of the see.
Whyte russette, or a gynger coloure.
A beaste called a graye, a brocke, or a badger.
A woman, who with her syster Amalthea, nourysshed Iupyter. It is also an herbe, commonly called baume.
An Ile lyeng betwene Italy and Epirus. Also a citie made by the Carthaginensis.
A drynke made of hony and must, or newe wyne.
Were praty littel houndes, in the which ladies toke plesure and delyte, whiche were brought out of the sayde yle of Melite.
A precyous stone of the colour of an orenge.
The name of hym, whiche dydde fyrst sacrifice vnto ydolles. also the name of an auuncient philosopher.
A hony man, or sellar of hony.
The tyme of driuynge of hyues, whan hony is taken out.
New must, wherin hony is sodden.
A mell dewe, whiche falleth on leaues of trees, and somtime on corne.
My hony, my sweetynge, a worde of wanton dalyers.
They which doo practyse dressynge of honye.
A warker or maker of hony.
The name of hym, whiche accused Socrates.
A confection made with honye clarifyed.
Of hony. also swete, as Vox mellea, a swete voyce.
A kynde of poulse, of the coloure of redde, of the fourme of Mylle.
He that syngeth cunnyngely, and swetely.
An yle by Sicile, in the whyche was great plenty of shepe.
Whan apples, very rype & fayre, be conserued in hony.
Parchement or velume, wherin men do write, also the ouermoste skynne of any thynge.
The setting or order of mēbres.
A lyttel tree lyke a citron tree.
The sonne of Thiton, whiche came to the ayde of the Troyans.
Byrdes, which were supposed to growe of the ashes of Mēnon.
A thynge, whiche shulde be remembred.
He that hath a good memory.
Parfitely by hart, or with good remembraunce.
To remembre, somtyme to tel, or expounde, to recite or reherse.
A lyttell fyshe, blacke in semer, and white in wynter.
The name of a comedy of Plaut.
Quene of Amazon, whom Hercules vaynquished.
People of the coūtrey called Gellarlande, or Gylderlande.
A famouse poete, a wryter of comedies.
An Ile in the see betwene Carthage and Sicile.
He or she, whiche is oute of her wytte.
A faulte or vice in wrytynge.
An offyce amonge the olde Italyans called Osci.
A byrde lyke to a small egle.
Buyldynge outewarde in prospectes or galeries.
An Ile agaynst the lasse Affrica.
The hyghest and chiefe parte of the mynde.
A table or bourd to eate on. somtime dyner or soupper.
The banker or exchaungeour, of whom men do borow money vpon gayne, called exchaunge.
That which hath floures lyke to women
A womans naturall purgation called floures.
The preuye membre of a manne.
A dyssease, whiche couereth all the face with a skurfe.
A dyssease, whiche infectith beastes with scabbes aboute theyr mouthes and lyppes.
The famous ryuer, whiche is now called Danubius.
For my cause, on my behalfe.
Condutes or ways, wherby any humour floweth.
A stenche or yl sauour, which procedeth of corrupt water or licour, mixt with erthe.

o: Meracus, ca, cum, et Merax, racis,
n: meracus ca cum et merax racis

d: Vendible, or that, which maye be bought.
Wages, the reward of labour or seruice.
That whiche is tourned in byenge and sellynge.
To bye for to sel for gaynes. sometymes to bie generally.
Was of the paynimes called god of Eloquence, and messager of Iupiter, it is the name of one of the seuen planettes.
The excrement or ordure of a man or beaste.
Meate eaten at after noone, a collataion, a none m • le.

To take wages, to deserue, to exercise a vile occupation. Mereor bene de te, I do somewhat for the, I d • serue to haue the my frende, or to haue thy fauour. Male mereor de te, I doo the displeasure, I do yll deserue thy fauour. Also Merere, to serue in warres. Merere stipendia, to take wagis as a souldyour, or to be a souldiour.
To lyue in brothelry, to playe the harlote.
Pitcheforkes for to take vp sheues.
Vines, or other small trees, whiche ar bowed and haue the toppes bowe wise tourned and set into the erthe.
An instrument where the matche of a lampe is conteyned.
A bukket to drawe vp water.
A waterfoule called a dyue doppar, some do call it a foule of the see lyke to a gull, whiche dyueth vnder the water to take fishe.
He that drynketh moch wyne without water.
To dyne, to eate meate at noone, to slepe at none.
A fygure called also dystributio, wherby the oration is distributed into sō dry sentences.
To be worthye, also to serue in warres.
That whiche is let or sette for aduantage.
A house wherinto a man is receyued for his money.
Howses or shoppes let to hyre.
A benefite, a deserte good or ylle.
A mountayne in the thirde part of Europa beyonde Grece.
An yle on the great ryuer of Nilus in Egipte.
Was in scorne the name of Nero, bicause he was so great a drynker of wyne.
She that drynkethe wyne without water.
A byrde which doth eate bees.
A lyttell stone of the coloure of leekes, whiche sweateth a lyckour lyke to mylke.
A moūtain in Grece by Thessaly.
A hylle of Inde, at the foote wherof is the citie callyd Nisa.
A ryuer whiche runneth by Braband and the lande of Luke and Gellar, called the Mase.
Entrees betwene the haule and the parlour.
A Countrey ioynynge to Hungrye, Myse.
He that plaieth on a flute or other pype in the myddes of the daunsers.
A drudge in a shyppe, or a shyp page, whiche dothe all vyle seruice in the shyppe.
A preciouse stone, blacke, hauynge a whyte strake in the myddes.
A whyte stone, hauyng a blacke lyne in the myddes.
A countreye lyinge betwene the two greatte ryuers Euphrates, and Tigris.
Wyfe to the emperour Claudius a woman of vnsaciable lechery.
Haruest, sometyme it sygnifieth the corne or the grapes newe mowen or gathered.
A but, or pricke to shote at, somtyme a marke or gowle in the felde, where vnto men or horses do runne, somtyme a boūde in landes. Also a reyke of corne or heye, also the lower part of a myll.
A promontory or mountayne lyinge into the see, whiche diuideth Affrica fro Numidia.
A fygure, whereby a worde is put from his commune signification.
They which do dygge and warke mettall out of the mynes, wherin mettall is founde.
A transformation or chaungynge of fygure.
A translation of wordes frome their propre sygnifycation.
A fygure callyd transformation. It is a translatyng of wordes being in prose into a fourme of meter, eyther for necessitie, or to augmente the elegancye.
A citie in the realme of Naples.
The transposyng of soules after the opinion of the Pythagoriens, out of one body into an other body.
Where one letter is transposed from one place in a worde into an nother as Tymber Tymbre.
A ryuer of Vmbria, whiche runneth into Flaminia.
The propre name of dyuers noble Romaynes.
He that is studious in suche speculation.
Are bokes of Aristotle, wherin he treateth of sterres, and suche other celestiall thynges.
A compendious or redy way, or a rule certayne to lerne by any science.
A fygure called denomination, as Bacchus for wyne, Venus for lechery, Cupido for loue.
A citie in the yle of Lesboe.
To mete or measure, to giue by measure, to passe ouer.
A towne in Grece called Modon.
To sette boundes, to measure lande, to dispose.
Oyle of almondes, also a tree in Affrica, whiche destylleth downe gumme lyke to rosyn.
He that consydereth a mās face, and therby iudgeth his condycions or affectes.
A measure for lyckour, whiche is also called Amphora, and contayned euery way square one foote.
The bishop of the chiefe citie.
To feare or dreade with tremblynge.
A citie in the part of Italy, callyd Vmbria, wherein Propertius the poete was borne.
A citie in wales called saint Dauid.
It is my duetie or my parte.

To glisten, or shyne. Diggnus qui cū in tenebris mices, is applied to one, whiche is reputed to be an honeste man, and a trusty, whiche wyll kepe touch and deceyue no man. It may be this wise translated, in a commune fourme of speakynge, He is one, with whom thou mayst assuredly bargayne. also to holde vp now one fynger, nowe two, as men do whanne they trete or bargain togyther by signes.
Curiositie aboute thynges of no valour.
A kynge of Phrigie, who excellyd all other in rychesse.
To remoue frome one place, to dwell in an other.
A man of warre, a souldiour.
Warre. sommetyme the exercise of warre.
To goo on warfare, or to be in warres.
A worme hauynge a great numbre of feete.
A myle, also a cawdron, also a pyller in Rome, wherein was grauen all the wayes of Italye.
A mastyues colar, made of lether with nayles.

The name of one, whiche at the game of Olimpus, with his bare hande, slewe a bulle, and after caried hym a furlonge, and the same daye eate hym euery morsel. It was also a noble Romayne, for whom Tullie made an oration, conteining incomparable eloquence.
A kyte. There is also a fyshe and a sterre of the same name.
Of a kyte, or lyke a kyte.
Women dedicate to the folishe ceremonies of Bacchus.

A bourder or rayler, which in mockynge other men in gesture and countenaunce, dothe folowe them, faynynge to be the same persones, whome they do reproue. Mimi, be verses counterfaytynge moche wantonnes without any reuerēce, hauynge not withstandynge somme wyse sentences myngled therwith.
A wryter of suche wanton matters.
Was the pounde of Athenes, which in weight cōtained .lxxv. dragmas: in money it conteined a hundred dragmas or olde poyse grotes, wherof .viii. wente to one ounce.
People in Arabia, nigh to the red see
Are of somme vsed for mynes, out of the which mettal is digged.
Called goddesse of doctryne and wysedom, which was also named Pallas.
A rewarde gyuen somtime by scholers vnto their maysters, in meate or drynke.
Leste. minime gentiū, leste in all mens opinions. sometyme minime signifieth no, in no wise. minime doctus vnlerned. minime sapiens, vnwyse. minime mirum, lyttell meruayle.
Limned bokes, hauyng letters of dyuers colours.
Seruice, sometyme generallye all warke. somtyme ministeria be seruātis.
To serue, to gyue a thynge in doinge seruyce.
The name of a citie in Sycile, of an other in the ile called Amorgos, by Sicile
Was the kynge of Crete, and gaue to theym lawes, whome paynyms for his excellente iustice, supposed to be chyefe Iudge of helle.
Was a monster kepte in Crete, halfe a man, halfe a bulle.
To synge smalle, or to feyne in syngynge.
A meate made with chopped herbes, a iussell.
A sellar of tryfles or smalle haberdashe ware.
The smallest thing that may be sene.
Mines, they be also vaynes of metall, out of the whiche is taken synope.
A miracle, a thynge excedynge nature, or commune reason.
To meruayle, to like a thing.
He that hateth the company of men.
To myxe or meddyll together, to confounde together, to trouble or to do a thynge out of order or reason, sometyme it sygnyfyeth to serue one with drynke.
He that dothe an acte of charytie on hym whom he pytieth.

Thynges whiche the auncient emperours were wonte to caste amonge the people, as breade, cakes, swete oyntemēt, and suche lyke thynges, which was done in the Theatre, in the feastes, called Saturnalia.
A message, also leaue to departe.
A course, whan one thynge commeth in a distance after a nother, a turne.
To omit or passe ouer a thing, also to gyue leaue to departe.
To waxe tame or quiet, somtyme to waxe rype.
The Persians do call the sonne, and also the chiefe priest of the sonne.
A stone of the colour of a rose, but agaynst the sonne he is chaungeable.
A puissaunt kynge of Ponthus in Asia.
A medicine lyke to tryakle, called Mitridate.
A citie in the ile of Lesbos.
A myter. It was also a tyre of womennes heedes.
To sende, to leaue or lay aparte, to gyue. Mirtere sanguinem, to let bloudde. Mittesanguis, a bloudde lettyng, or a bloudshede.
An Iyle syxe dayes saylynge oute of Englande, wherein is greatte plentie of tynne.
Forgyue me that faute.Cice. pro Cluencio. Asc. Ped.
To lette the iuges departe to gyue sentence, after that the oratour hath finished his oration, or the lawyer his plee.
A cuppe, wherin wyne is alayde with water.
A citie of Araby. also the name of oone of the sonnes of Loth, of whom the peple are called Moabtae.

o: Modero•, aris, ari, et Modero, are,
n: modero aris ari et modero are
d: To gouerne, to rule, to sette a measure in thynges, to moderate.
Which excedeth not, measurable, sometyme lyttell or fewe.
To take the measure of a thynge.
A buckette, where with water is drawen out of a well: or a pot fastned to a whele, whiche bryngeth vp water, & poureth it out.
Men ordeyned to see measure kepte.
A bushell: it was proprelye a measure of daye thynges, whiche conteyned .xvi. Sextarios, vide postea in sextario.
Newe, nowe late, somtyme it signyf •• th so that. Non resert, modo id faciat, It maketh no mattier, soo that he doo it, also ••• ly.
To make or doo a thynge by numbre and measure, also to synge.
A songe, a modulation, the tyme in syngynge.
Maner, measure, furme, facion, way, quantite,Ci. ad At. Columel. ende. Etsi nihil scripsit, nisi de modo agri, although he wrote nothyng but of the quantitie of the felde.
Walles of a towne or castell.
To make one sadde and heuy.
A prouince in Asia nygh to Pontus.
A countreye in Asia, called nowe Cesaria.
A noble Citie in Germany, called Mense.
A myl, it is also a great pece of fleshe without shape, growen in a woman, whiche causeth them somtyme to thynke, that they be with chylde, it is also a cake made of mele and salte.

o: Molaris, re, et Molarius, ia, um,
n: molaris re et molarius ia um

d: An horse, whiche dryueth about a malte myll.
A thynge that is verye greatte and weightye: sommetyme it is taken for diffycultie.
A garment which was myxt with some mater, whiche gathered fyre, putte on some persones that shulde suffre deathe.
To greue, to offende, to do displeasure to one.
That whiche greueth, offendeth, or discontenteth.
A morter or querne, wherin any thynge maye be grounde with the hande.
That whiche we go about and endeuour vs to do.

To moue, to be moued, or styrted to doo a thynge. moliri classem, to prepare a nauy. moliri iter, to perfourme a iourneye. moliri habenas, to rule. moliri insidias, to laye snares, to laye in awayte. Moliri arcem, to buylde a fortresse. Moliri bellum, to make warre. Moliri is somtime to deuyse or inuent, also to go about to do a thynge, to make, to be taryed or lette.
To waxe softe, to be pacified from wrathe.
To make softe or tender, to pacific or appayse, to make wanton or tēder.

Softe, tender. molle ingenium, a wit whiche lyghtely taketh. mollis homo, a man effemynate, or womanly, not hardye or constant of wytte, inuolued an wanton pleasures and sensuall appetite, somtyme mollis sygnifieth rype, also remisse, sometyme pleasaunt, also easy to be pleased.
Gentylly with good wylle, easily, delycately.
A nutte with a softe shale, a fylberde.
A colour like to the floures of mallowes.
A plumrule, suche as masons and carpenters doo occupie in squarynge of stone and tymber.
People in the parte of Grece called Epirus.
A mastiue dogge. it is also a fote in meter.
A square piece of tymber, wheron the paynyms dyd sacrifyce. It is also the trendyll of a myll. Also the swellynge of a womans bealy, whiche dothe happen as well to maidens, as to wyues.
An herbe called also Plūbago, it is also the oore of leade or syluer.
The spume or fome of leade.
That whyche durethe but a lyttell whyles, or shortly altereth.
That whiche is done in a lyttell space.
The leste parte of tyme, which can not be assigned, a moment.
To contente hym, whom almoste nothynge may please.
To contende afore a rigorous and extreme iudge.
A solytarie person, all be it that it is vsed for a monke.
A prynce, whiche reuleth alone without piere or companyon, monarche.
A byrde callydde a Choughe or Cadesse.
To warne, to putte in remembraunce.
He that warneth a man, or putteth hym in remembraunce.
Money, also the name of Iuno.
A maker of money, a coyner.
A colar or bee, whiche women vse to weare aboute their neckes, It is also a poytrell of a horse.
That whiche doth warne, or exhorte.
An Ile pertaynynge to Englande, whiche some do suppose to be Angle sey, somme Manne, betwene Lancaster and Irelande.
They whiche haue a longe thing lyke to spyttes. Also they that be veraye hyghe in personnage and aboue other. Lampridius in uita Alex.
An Instrumente, hauynge manye strynges of oone sowne, sauynge that with smalle pieces of cloth, the sonnes be distincte, as Clauycordes be.
A man hauynge but one eye.
A lamentable or mournyng song, suche as is songen in funeralles.
Was a manne, whyche in stede of teethe, hadde but oone boone, lyke as kynge Pirrhus hadde.
He that neuer hadde but one wyfe.
A longe tale of one mattier.
A battayle, wherein oonely two menne doo fyghte.
A meale of one onely meate or dyshe.
A table sette on one foote or trestylle.

Where one manne ingrosseth thynges, to haue all in his owne hande, that no manne maye gayne, but he onely. It maye be also one countrey or market, that taketh away the gaynes from other countreyes or markettes.
A worde hauyng but one case.
Men in India, whiche haue but one legge, so greate, that therwith they couer them selfes from the sonne.
Where as is but one pyller.
A bote made in oone piece of tymber.
A monster, that which excedeth or lacketh in naturall fourme or order.

A remembrance of some notable acte, as sepulchres, images, pylars, grete stones, inscriptions, bookes, and other lyke: whereby any thinge excellent, concernynge grete wittes, kunnynge, entreprise in armes, puyssaunce, or rychesse is remembred.
The name of saynct Austens mother.
A gyant, one of the Centaures.
The wyfe of kynge Mithridate, whiche after that her husbande was vainquisshed, killed her selfe.
That which causeth discase or sickenesse.
A vice inueterate and harde to be cured, as ambition, auarice.
He that doeth byte, be it with the teeth, or with langage.
To byte, to detract, or rebuke vehemently.
To gnawe on the brydell, which is spoken where it signifieth one to repugne against seruitude or bondage.
Bytinge harde and faste, as a man holdeth a thinge.
To holde fast, to persist obstinately in an opinion or sentence.
To obaye, to do as a man bedeth, to conforme one mannes maners to anothers.
People in fraunce, dwellynge about Turwan.

n: morior iris amp eri moriri amp mori

d: He that speketh treatably, somtyme wordes treatably spoken: sometyme it signifieth him, that speketh foolyshely.
To tary or abyde, to let, or cause to tary.
Waywarde, dyuerse in condicions, whome no man can please, more curiouse than nedeth.
A madnesse or frenesy, where a man loseth his memory.
A bytt with the teeth, a taunt in spekinge.
A mortar, wherin thinges are, brayed or grounden.
Moren fleshe, whiche dyeth by it selfe, carrayne.
Cornes which be on mennes fete.
Which causeth any thinge to dye.
A grete mere in Syria, where in no heuy thinge may synke.
A Mulbery tree, and a brembyl that beareth blacke beryes.
A maner, a cōdiciō, also custome.
Pearis, whiche do sauoure lyke muske,
A Region in Asia nyghe to the ryuer of Phasis, deuyded into thre partis, in the one doo dwell people called Colchi, in the second Hiberes, in the third Armenii.
The great captayn of the iewes which lad them out of Egipte.
People in Asia towarde the north.
To moue, to remoue or put away
To slyre or allure the minde.
To do thynges to be lamented.
To stere thinges, which shall be to his owne displeasure, that begynneth it.
Fylth, vinue, suche as is on bred or meate longe kept.
The point of a sworde or knife. sometyme it is taken for a sworde.
The fylthe, whyche commeth oute of the nose.
To bellowe lyke a cowe or bull▪ somtyme it signifyeth the noyse of thunder, or grete wyndes.
A gate at Rome, whereby catell dyd entre into the citie.
Bellowynge of kyne, or other noyse lyke.
To pacyfye, to appease, to mitigate, to make sweete, to anoynte, to polyshe.
One of the names of Vulcane, called god of fyre.
A penaltie, a condemnation, a fyne sessed.
To forfayte, to runne in the peyne.
The mylkyng, the payle, wherinto it is milked, which is also called Mulctrale.
Certayne shooes of purple coloure, whiche the kynges of Alba ware, and afterwarde the noble men of Rome.
Forkes, wheron fardels were trussed and borne by men.

A prouerbe referred vnto thē, whiche be obedient to euery commaundment, be it neuer so greuouse. It may also be applied vnto thē, which be inuolued in perpetuall and intollerable laboures and businesse.
Mules do gnappe one an other, a prouerbe applied to persones ylle and defamed, whan one of them commendeth the other.
A woman, proprely she that is no virgine.
Naturall euacuations, which women haue, called their floures.
A folower, or dotar on women.
To effeminate, or make lyke a woman.
A dryuer of Mules, a muletour.
Pertayning to a forfait, or payne assessyd.
A part representinge an infinite quantitye. Quam paruula pars, quam multesima constat, so lytle a porcion, se of how wonderfull gretnesse it is.
He that hath moche heare on his bearde.
To make moche of, to esteme moche.
Garmentes made of fyne thredes or sylke.
To punysshe, to condemne, to put fro, to intreate yl, or disorder.
He that maketh a cōmune game or playe at his propre charges.

n: muneror aris ari amp munero are

d: To make clene, proprely ones nose.
Priuately or particulerly, belonginge to one citie.
The priuate lawe of euery particuler citie.
Ciuile offices in euery citie or towne.
A citie or towne incorporate, hauynge their propre officers and lawes.
A citezen, or burgeyse, enioyinge the liberties of the towne.
Liberall, Munificentior, more liberall, Munificentissimus, most liberall. in the olde tyme Munifici, were taken for them, whyche consented to that, whiche theyr frendes dyd or spake.
A fortifycation of a towne or castelle.
To fortifye, to prepare, to repayre.
He that beareth the charges, which the people shulde do.

A gylt, a charge, a duetie or offyce. Munera, commune playes and gaye sightes for the peple to behold, to reioice them, prepared by officers of cities. As in Rome, sondry playes, sworde players, called Gladiatores, huntyng of wyld beastes. Also now in the citie of London, the watches & syghtes on midsomer nightes.
Smalle chaynes, whiche women do weare.
A garlande gyuen to hym, whiche in the siege of a citie fyrste skalyd the walles, and entred.
An herbe callyd perytorye, or pelytorie.
A shelle fyshe, of whome commeth the lycour, whyche maketh purple colour. Sometyme it sygnifyeth the same coloure. Also an herbe, whiche groweth in a pyt, where no sonne shyneth.
A countrey in the southe partes of Spayne.
Water, wherin salt is sodden, brine.
Caltrappes, lyke thre yron pryckes so ioyned, that beinge throwen, one standethe vpryghte, vsed in battayle for horsemenne.
Where oone gothe fearefully, as if he went on caltraps or thornes
A mouse killer, a fole, a rat killer.
A bryne made with salte sodden in water.
Targettes, wherewith men faught vpon walles.
To murmour, or make noyse lyke to water.
A stone of dyuers colours, clere as cristall, hauynge spottes purple & whyte.
Of that stone called murrha, wherof cuppes, pottes, tables, and other vessels were made: there be of them dyuers sent from Venyce.
Was wyne made with dyuers spices, as that which is callyd ypocras.
A hylle atte Rome, callyd also Auentinus.
One of the names of Venus.

Muses, were maydens, whome poetes fayned to be the doughters of Iupiter and Memorie, and that they were ladyes and gouernours of poetrie & musyke, whiche were in numbre nyne. Some call them gyuers of eloquence, and doo name them goddesses.
Be warkes cunnyngely paynted, that they seme to be in some place imbocid out, in som place grauen, although it be all playne.
An auncient poete, whiche was in the tyme of Orpheus, & was one of them whiche went with Iason to the wynninge of the fliece of golde.
A house, whervnto lerned men in all sciences vsed to repayre, and dispute: it is also a house dedicate to the musis.
A flappe to dryue away flyes. It is also the toppe of fenelle, dylle, and suche other like herbes, wherin be the seedes.
A certayne Rose, that springeth of a stalke with many smal braunches, and hath leaues lyke to an olyue tree.
A beaste, whiche beareth muske, a muske catte.
A trappe, wherwith myse or rattes are taken.

A lyttell mouse. Sommetyme an engyne of warre, whereby they are defended, whiche doo approche the walles of a place besyeged, to fylle the dyches, It is also a lyttell fyshe, whiche guydeth the whale that he do not runne on rockis.
Be certayne pieces of harde fleshe compacte with synewes in the body, whiche do inclose the spirituall membres.
Mosse, whiche groweth in welles and moyste places, sommetyme on trees, specially in colde countreyes.
A manne speakynge to hym selfe priuily.
To talke softely and secretely, to kepe sylence.
A tree hauynge leaues lyke to laurell, but greatter and weaker.
A lyttell instrumente made with two rules, betwene whiche the showe is put, whyles the sole is in sowynge.
A caa • e or paste made to comforte the stomacke.
A beaste called a wesell. also a fishe lyke a lampraye.
Newe wyne, newe ale, newe beere.

n: muteo mutui tere amp mutesco scere

d: Horned beastes, of nature lackynge hornes, as oxen, gotes. &c.
To cutte of, to mynyshe, to take awaye.
A naturall colour, as wull or clothe neuer dyed.
To speake softely, or with an vnperfyt voyce, to muttre.
Scaffolde holes, or places made on the walles for culuers to brede in.
To chaunge, to translate, to barter one thinge for an other.
The priuie membre of a man.
Togither, or one an other, Mutuó diligebant, They loued one an other.
Sygnyfieth bothe to borowe and to lende.
A lone, that whiche is borowed.
Mutuall loue, where one loueth an nother equally.
A shel fishe in the see called Bosphorus, whiche bryngeth forth lytell redde stones, and rounde.
A citie in the parte of Grecia, called Peloponesus, and a lyttell region, where Agamemnon raigned, the chiefe capitayne of the grekes agaynste Troy, called nowe Morea.
The name of a famous paynter.

A syckenesse of the eyes, where no colour of the eies ar changed, but maketh them moche broder: all be it it taketh away the syght, or maketh a man to se the lasse, and the thynges, whiche be sene, to seme lasse than they are.

A part of Macedonia on the see syde, where Niobe was tourned in to a stoone. Aristotle saythe, that it is a parte of Phrigia, ioynynge to Lidia. Solynus sayth, that it was called Bebrycia, and after Bythinia.
A butterfly, whiche is in mylles.
A kynde of shyppes vsed in the see called Mare Tirrhenum.
A tourners pynne or spyndelle, wheron he turneth or warketh any thing.
A citie in Licia, wherof saynte Nycholas was byshoppe.
A captayn of ten thousand mē.
A lyttell bushe called in Italye Tamarico.
The male kynde of a lampray, whiche hath a tothe out of his mouthe.
A stone, wherin is the fygure of an emotte.
A kynd of spiders, lyke an emote hauyng a black bealy with white spottes.
Were sworde players, where the one prouoked the other to battayle.
A kynd of fenell, hauyng gretter leaues, and a sharper taste.
A towne in the part of Grece, callyd Peloponesus.
A lytell beaste, which deuoureth emotes.

A fruite growinge in India, lyke vnto plummes or damsyns, whereof be dyuers kyndes, which easily do purge al superfluous humours, and also comforteth nature, in so moche as a manne, whiche eateth them, beinge condite, shall not loke oldely.
They whiche do make swete oyntmentes.
The name of an excellent carner. also olde oyle.
A place where oyntementes were solde.
A place, where Myrtelle trees be sette.
A porcyon of the see, whiche is betwene the sees called Aegeum & Ioniū.
A lyttell tree, bearynge bearyes of swete odour.
The name of a cunnyng grauer. also a shelle fyshe of the see.
A countrey beyonde Hungarye, toward Grece. Ptholomeus writeth of two countreys called Mysia, the more and the lasse, and both in Asia, beyonde Bythinia, not farre from Ida.
Mysteries, thynges secrete or hid in wordes or ceremonies.
A fyshe called a see mouse.
A declaration or exposytion of fables.
The fylthe whiche commeth oute of a mannes nose.
The name of a certayne citie.
A countreye betwene the redde see and the see callyd Persicum, contayning with in it Arabie.
In the langage of Ethiope, is a beest hauyng a heed lyke a camell, a necke lyke a hors, legges and fete lyke an oxe.
An instrument of musyke, called a psaltrie.
The participle of Nansciscor, Nactus sum, I haue gotten, nactus es, nactus est, thou, he hath gotten.

Sygnifieth valde, or nimis. Nae tu homo facetus es, thou arte a very mery felowe. somtyme it signifieth Certè, profectó, ita. Nae illi vehementer errant, surelye they be farre out of the waye. Nae ego multo libē tius emerim diuorsoriū Tarracinae, In good faythe I had leauer haue bought a howse at Tarracine.
A mournynge songe, wont to be songen at burielles, somtyme it signifieth the sōge that the mother or norice doth singe dandyllynge of her chylde.
A mole or lyke marke in the body or face, from the tyme of the byrthe.
Fayries, of the ryuers and fountaynes.
A riuer, whiche cometh out of the hil called Taurus, and runneth in to the see called Pontus.
To get or opteyne. sometyme to fynde.
Verily, truely: if it be sette afore other wordes: if it be putte after, it sygnifyeth for.
Called goddesses of flowres and woddes.
People in the yle called Lesbos.
A kynd of pitche, also lyme, wherwith fyre is nourished.
A place where Nauewes be sowen.
The south part of Fraūce wherin is Dolphinay, Prouance, Langedok. &c.

A flowre in facion lyke a lyllye, and whyte, sauing that the chalese, wherin the floure is closed, is purpleisome haue purple floures, leaues narower than leke blades, a stalke halfe a foote hygh, plaine without leaues, a rounde rote and white. Also the name of a yonge man of excellēt beautie, who for the loue of a maid ē died, and after the fables of poetes, was transfourmed into the same lylly.

A qualytie or vertue in thynges to make a manne to slepe. also to make a membre insensible. Physytions vse medycines, whyche haue this vertue, where the griefe or ache is otherwise incurable, or where they wylle cutte any parte of a mannes bodye.
The name of a swete oyntment.
The herbe and rote, whiche is called Spikenarde.
The name of a lyttell fyshe, whiche dothe swymme very swyftely.
An yle in the see called Aegeum.
A citie of the people named Locri in Grece.
A narration or report of thynges that are doone.
A place, wherein medycines are kepte.
A stone of coloure languyne, hauynge blacke vaynes.
The surname of one of the Scipions a noble Romayne.
A water vessell, wyde aboue, hauynge handelles.
A fyshers weele or bow nette, wherin if a fyshe be ones, he can not gette out.
A nose: somtime sharpenes in speche, and tauntynge wytte. also iudgement in letters.
Taunters, checkers, skorners, somtyme wytty personnes, whiche do quikly perceyue a thynge. also men, which haue their priuie membres very great.
A tauntynge wenche, or a shrewe.

o: Natalis, le, et natalitius, tia, tium,
n: natalis le et natalitius tia tium
d: The daye of birthe or natiuitie.
Is taken for progeny or dyscente, or bloude. Generosi natales, gentyl bloud. Obscuri natales, a poore dyscente or lowe byrthe, somtyme it is vsed for yeres.
Where a man hath armes and tytle of nobylitie,Budeus. gyuen vnto hym by the kynge.
A place wherin men do swymme.
Trauaylours, or they whiche haue moche businesse.
Where a thyng is borne or begon.
To swymme, sometyme to go, to tremble, to sayle, or rowe.
A water serpēt. also an herbe, whose rote smelleth lyke a gote.
Nature, membres of generacyon. Sometyme facion or maner.
The docke where shyps be laid vp.
A docke or place where shyppes are made.
A countrey in Spayne called Nauarre.
A nutte shale, a thynge of naughte.
A holowe tree lyke a shyppe, whiche is occupied whan grapes be gathered.
To rowe or be rowed in a bote for salace.
Where a shyppe maye passe, Nauigable.
A iourneye or goinge by water in a shyppe.
The pilate of a shyppe, whych ruleth the sterne.
The leadynge or settynge forth of the shyppe. It is also all kynde of vesselles to sayle or rowe in.
To sayle or rowe, that is to say, to be caried on water in a shippe or any other thynge lyke.
A shyppe whiche serueth onely for pleasure, hauynge chaumbers and bankettynge tables for greate men to solace in.
The fraite or fare paied for passage
Battayle on the See, also the place where the batayle is.
They which do fyght on the see or water in shyppes or botes.
To accomplyshe dylygentely, to gyue, to applye with effect, to be in ayde. Iam mihi videor nauasse operam ꝙ huc venerim, nowe me seemeth I haue well applyed my labour, that I am come hyther.
A ryuer, whiche passeth out of Slauony.
The abhorrynge of thynges seene, wherby a man is prouoked to vomyte.
To be dysposed to vomyte, somtyme to vomyte.
Was doughter to Alcinous, kyng of Phaeaces, whiche founde Vlysses, whan he escaped from drounynge, and brought hym to her father.
To open or gape as a beane doth whan he spryngeth.
The sonne of Neptunus, and father of Alcinous.
An hiue made of the facion of a shyppe.
Curriers bleche or lycour, also the stynkynge water, which issueth out of the pumpe of a shyppe.
A shypman, also a fyshe, which is in similitude lyke to some that sayled.
An yle in the see called Aegeum.
A man consecrate or dedycate to god. Nazarei were men, which had made vowes vntyll a certayne tyme.
A citie in Cappadotia, afterwarde called Caesaria.

An aduerbe, signifieng forbeading or dissuading. Tu ne cede malis, giue thou not place to aduersitie or mysaduentures. sometyme it is a coniunction copulatiue, and signifieth nor or. neyther. somtime rational, and signifieth wherfore. somtyme causal, & signifieth not. somtyme leste, also or not, whither. somtyme it is an interrogatiue. Ego ne? I trowest thou?
But to be short,Cice. 〈◊〉 Cluend • , & in Ve • . Ci. • C • . what nedeth any longer tale, to make a short tale.
In fewe wordes. Ne multis Diogenes emitur, In fewe wordes Diogenes is bought.
I wold I lyued not. Ne viuā si tibi concedo, I wolde I lyued not, or I wold I shulde not liue, if I graunt that to the.Cicero.

Not onely, somtyme nor yet, where the thynge of least estimation is put laste. Nedum, sygnifieth not onely, as Fundere pro te sanguinem, nedū pecuniam, I wolde spende for the not only my money, but also my bloode. where the thinge of moost estimation is last put, it signifieth nor yet. Ne crederem tibi obulum, nedum vitā meam, I wyll not commytte my lyfe vnto thy credēce, nor yet lende the one halfepeny.
Feastes in the honour of Bacchꝰ, also skinnes of dere wherwith they were clad which kept the ceremonies of Bacchꝰ
An hyl in Sicile, where there is great plentie of falowe dere.
A vapour or myst rysynge from the water, whiche eyther tourneth forthwith into a cloude, or shortly vanysheth.
A house where corne is thresshed, or wynn owed in tyme of rayne.
A thefe, a knaue, a lewde person, or vacabunde.
Of force, it must nedꝭ be.
Nede, necessitie. sometime a bonde of frendship or kynrede.
The olde writers vsed for nec cum, nor with.
In the olde Spanyshe tungue was the image of Mars, garnyshed with beames lyke the sonne, it also signyfied in latyne mas, the male kynde.
A sylke worme, whan he is yōge sprounge out of the sede.
Slayne without weapon, as with poyson, famyne, prisonement.
A Necromancer, or caller vp of yll spirites.
The drinke of goddes, somtime it signifieth immortalitie.
Horrible, not to be spokē or named.
A cursed dede, a wycked thynge, execrable, detestable.
Dayes whan it is not lefull.
To neglect, to haue lyttel regarde.
To deny, to refuse, to say not.
Say that she wyl not go.
To practyse marchaundyse, to be occupied in businesse.
He that is moch occupied with businesse.
A marchaunte, he that is busied in an other mans affaires.
Perteynyng to businesse, occupation, or trouble.
Remedye. Omnis res palam est, ne que vllum pol de hac re negotium est, quin male occidam, All the matter is knowen: therfore in this case in faith there is no remedy, but that I wyll kyll hym.
Full of businesse, care, or trouble of mynde.
Businesse, occupation, somtyme trouble, care, or labour of mynde.
A factour or sollicitor in a mannes busynesse.
The father of duke Nestor, whiche was at the siege of Troye.
Was vsed of old writers for somtime, also for but, or excepte.
A greate wodde, where Hercules slewe an horrible lyon.
Of the wodde callyd Nemeae, whiche is in Grecia, not farre frome the citie of Argos.
A goddesse, whiche was supposed to take vengeance on malefactours. some tyme it sygnifieth fortune, also iustyce, also reproche.
Nymphes or maydens of the see.
Is applied to hym that dare not speke. Ne my quidem facere audet, He dare not ones mutte, or make coūtenance to speake.
Is an aduerbe confyrming a thing. for bycause, surely, verily, sometyme for.
A wod for pleasure, wherin deere or other beastes may fede.
The fyrst day of the newe mone.
A newe man, or a plante newely sproungen.
Is in englishe a new knight, It was also the name of Pirthꝰ the sonne of Achilies.
He that is nowe, or was of late tyme.
A drynke or an herbe, whiche causeth a man to forgete heuynesse. Also the herbe called dorago.
A citie of the countrey of Thuscane in Italy.
Feastes wherin no wyne was sacryfysed or drunke, but onely mede, and they were called the feastes of sobre men.
A cloude, also the name of a womanne, whiche was mother of Helles, who gaue the name to the see callydde Hellespontus.
Peyn in the raynes of the backe.
An herbe called nepe, or calament.
The sonne or doughters sonne, sometyme a waster of goodes, a riottouse person. Nepotes, do sometyme signify all the discent, whiche commeth after a mans sonnes or daughters.
A dimynutiue of Nepos. Meus Nepotulus, my lyttell sonne, or yonge son, from the fyrst discent.
The doughter of a mans sonne or doughter.
A noughty felowe, a manne to be nothinge estemed.
In no wyse, not a whitte.
Nothyng to to, that is to say, moche excedynge, or moche lackynge.
To be wanton, also to denie.
